retrieval_policy: Offline text packets; source URLs and images not needed at design time.

screens.name: Voice task capture
screens.layout: Detected tasks appear as separate rows with completion circles and small scheduling metadata. A listening state and waveform sit below the growing list; cancel and confirmation controls frame the capture operation.
screens.lesson: Show recognized structured output while an input operation is still active.

screens.name: Project calendar with task sheet
screens.layout: A multi-day calendar places all-day items above timed blocks. An opened task sheet overlays the lower portion, showing task identity, project, date and assignee while retaining the calendar as context.
screens.lesson: Use a contextual detail layer without replacing the user's time reference.

screens.name: Workspace and project navigation
screens.layout: Profile and utility actions precede grouped Inbox, Today and Upcoming destinations. Personal and team sections use expandable hierarchy; project folders and children share aligned leading symbols and trailing actions.
screens.lesson: Separate personal navigation from shared workspace hierarchy without duplicating the entire shell.

screens.name: Task display configuration
screens.layout: A top-level layout choice uses three visual options. Below it, completion settings and sorting/grouping values occupy distinct row groups. Cancel and confirm flank the sheet title.
screens.lesson: Give representation choices a visual preview while keeping secondary display controls compact.

screens.name: Workspace home navigation
screens.layout: Recent pages appear in a horizontal tile strip above a Favorites tree. Nested pages indent beneath their parent, with expand controls leading and create actions trailing; workspace identity remains at the top.
screens.lesson: Combine fast re-entry with a predictable hierarchy for less frequent destinations.

screens.name: Personal wiki directory
screens.layout: A cover and page icon precede a prominent title. Small section headings divide linked pages into personal categories, with one text link per row and restrained utility actions in the top bar.
screens.lesson: A useful directory can use editorial grouping instead of repeated large cards.

screens.name: Travel database list
screens.layout: A page icon and title lead into a compact view toolbar. Trip rows pair a leading symbol and destination with a secondary date range, separated by fine horizontal rules.
screens.lesson: Keep the primary object and its most useful discriminator together in each row.

screens.name: Notes database list
screens.layout: The page title and database controls occupy the top area. A dense list of note titles uses small leading icons and quiet row separators; creation, search and view options stay in the same toolbar.
screens.lesson: Preserve room for real titles by keeping database chrome compact.

screens.name: Checklist editing with keyboard
screens.layout: The document contains a title, an explanatory callout and checkable text rows. A compact formatting strip sits immediately above the visible keyboard, keeping editing controls near the active content.
screens.lesson: Adapt editing tools to the keyboard state without replacing document context.

screens.name: Initiative project list
screens.layout: A back control and utilities sit above initiative identity and view tabs. Projects are grouped by lifecycle stage; each row pairs a small identity symbol with a trailing status indicator. Navigation remains at the bottom.
screens.lesson: Make grouping carry the hierarchy so individual rows can stay compact.

screens.name: Priority inbox with row action
screens.layout: Inbox identity and utilities lead into priority tabs. Avatar-based entries combine a strong event title with lighter supporting text. One row exposes an unread action while adjacent notifications remain visible.
screens.lesson: Contextual row actions should not require a separate management screen.

screens.name: Project-aware assistant conversation
screens.layout: A compact conversation header precedes a contextual prompt card and a response status. The composer includes attachment and mention controls above the keyboard, while the current project context remains visible in the conversation.
screens.lesson: Keep the object being discussed visible while the user asks follow-up questions.

screens.name: New issue editor
screens.layout: A large title and freeform description dominate the screen. Status, priority, assignee and platform appear as compact chips above a formatting toolbar and keyboard; close and submit occupy opposite top corners.
screens.lesson: Move secondary metadata out of the main writing area while keeping it directly editable.

screens.name: Project overview and properties
screens.layout: Project identity and view tabs precede a short description. Property chips form a compact cluster, followed by separate sections for initiatives, resources and customer requests, with a persistent bottom navigation bar.
screens.lesson: Use distinct property and relationship sections instead of one undifferentiated metadata list.

screens.name: Workspace messaging home
screens.layout: Workspace identity and search occupy the header. Three shortcut tiles precede unread direct messages and expandable channel groups; a compose action and bottom navigation remain separated from the content list.
screens.lesson: Keep high-frequency destinations prominent without turning all navigation into equal tiles.

screens.name: Small group huddle
screens.layout: The channel and participant count sit above two prominent participant tiles. A low control row separates microphone, camera, reaction and chat actions; labels identify participants directly on their tiles.
screens.lesson: Give people and call controls separate visual zones.

screens.name: Channel with video and document
screens.layout: A channel header frames a conversation containing a video preview, author/time metadata and a document attachment card. Reactions stay beneath the message, and the composer anchors the bottom edge.
screens.lesson: Let attachment anatomy vary by content type while preserving common conversation alignment.

screens.name: Channel reaction state
screens.layout: Author avatars and timestamps organize the thread. Reaction pills sit below their associated message and wrap when needed; a repeated add-reaction affordance follows existing reactions, above the persistent composer.
screens.lesson: Keep lightweight feedback attached to the exact message it describes.

screens.name: Task destination index
screens.layout: A search field leads into standard task destinations with trailing counts. Thin separators distinguish personal and work project groups; project rows are quieter than the main time-based destinations.
screens.lesson: Use visual weight to distinguish navigation classes without adding extra containers.

screens.name: Today agenda and tasks
screens.layout: The Today heading precedes a compact appointment summary. Checkbox tasks follow with lighter project labels, while an evening subheading creates a second time group; a small creation action occupies the lower edge.
screens.lesson: Combine scheduled commitments and flexible tasks without pretending they are identical items.

screens.name: Upcoming task schedule
screens.layout: Large day numbers and weekday labels partition the list. Appointments precede tasks within each day; a highlighted task row remains legible against neighboring entries, with a creation action near the bottom.
screens.lesson: Anchor rescheduling around clear date groups and stable row anatomy.

screens.name: Task entry with subtasks
screens.layout: A rounded editor overlays a dimmed background above the keyboard. Title and note precede a short checklist, tag and scheduling controls; destination and save action share the bottom of the editor.
screens.lesson: Keep a small object's full creation context in one bounded editor.

screens.name: Project checklist sections
screens.layout: A project title and explanatory paragraph lead into named task sections. Checkbox rows include small note and progress indicators; section actions align with headings, and a creation affordance appears within the task area.
screens.lesson: Use meaningful headings to organize a long checklist before adding more navigation.

screens.name: Task notes with nested lists
screens.layout: A task title begins with an unchecked box, followed by an introductory note. Three numbered destinations contain indented bullet lists, with emphasized names and a closing paragraph. A compact row of calendar, tag, checklist, and flag icons sits below the note.

screens.name: Inbox grouped by date
screens.layout: The visible Inbox panel places menu and overflow buttons above its title. A rounded Today group contains four task rows, each beginning with a checkbox and ending with a scheduled time. Another group starts below, but its content is obscured by the publisher composition.

screens.name: Daily calendar agenda
screens.layout: The foreground calendar panel shows a month label and Today heading above a horizontal sequence of dates. The selected date is enclosed in a circle. Below it, a vertical time rail aligns with stacked appointment cards containing time ranges and task names.

screens.name: Habit tracking list
screens.layout: A Habit heading sits between utility icons, above weekday initials and a horizontal date row. The selected date is circular. Habit rows pair leading pictograms with names, optional progress text, and right-aligned total-day counts. The visible rows include exercise, water, reading, and daily check-in.

screens.name: Countdown list
screens.layout: The visible Countdown panel has a centered title and an overflow button. Each rounded row places a pictogram and event name on the left, with a large number and Days Until or Days Since label on the right. The publisher enlarges the Birthday row over neighboring rows.

screens.name: Daily task timeline
screens.layout: A date heading and seven-day strip occupy the top of the visible app. Small all-day items sit above a vertical schedule. Each timed task connects to the time rail through an icon, with its time range above the task name and a completion circle opposite. Navigation and add controls sit below.

screens.name: AI scheduling prompt
screens.layout: The screen opens with a greeting and a question about scheduling. Most of the body remains empty. A prompt composer near the bottom contains entered text, a microphone icon, and a Generate button. The app's bottom bar contains navigation icons alongside a separate circular add control.

screens.name: Week strip with agenda
screens.layout: A month-and-year heading sits above a compact weekday strip containing dates and event markers. Below the strip, the agenda is grouped under Today and Tomorrow headings, with weather information opposite. Event rows show times, names, and occasional locations; a meeting row includes a Join button.

screens.name: Calendar subscription catalog
screens.layout: A back button and centered Popular title head a list of calendar sources. Rows use leading circular icons with source names and trailing add buttons or chevrons. One expanded Moon Phases section contains a Subscribe button and a horizontal event-preview card with pagination dots underneath.

screens.name: Calendar weather detail
screens.layout: A back control and Weather title appear above a large current temperature and weather symbol. Location and near-term conditions follow. A sunrise-to-sunset arc separates this summary from a forecast-provider link. Beneath it, daily forecast columns show dates, condition icons, temperatures, and sunrise and sunset times.

screens.name: Month calendar with agenda
screens.layout: A month heading precedes a seven-column date grid with small event markers and a selected date. The agenda begins below a divider, grouping appointments under Today and Tomorrow. Times sit above event titles, secondary details follow, and one meeting includes a trailing Join button.

screens.name: Travel document overview
screens.layout: Back, share, and overflow controls sit above a document card. A wide cover photograph precedes the trip title, a centered subtitle, and supporting text. A checklist block follows with one completed item. Image-backed day cards form two columns below, followed by a wider third card.

screens.name: Task list with action menu
screens.layout: The Tasks screen has account and utility icons above four compact view tabs, with Today selected. An Inbox section contains checkbox rows with dates beneath several titles. A contextual menu overlays the right side, offering schedule, deadline, reminder, completion, cancellation, and open actions.

screens.name: Document publishing panel
screens.layout: The document header contains a back button, title, folder label, share icon, and overflow control. A sheet covers the lower document, with Share, Publish, Export, and Transfer tabs. Publish is selected above a Publish to the Web heading, explanatory text, and a miniature page preview.

screens.name: Calendar with daily notes and tasks
screens.layout: A Calendar heading sits between account and utility controls. The selected day's date and Today label introduce a note preview and a series of checkbox tasks, with source labels and deadline chips aligned to the right. Additional dated groups follow below, above the fixed navigation bar.

screens.name: Content collection board
screens.layout: The foreground app view has a back control, collection title, breadcrumb, and overflow button. A Status Management selector sits above side-by-side board columns labeled Idea and Draft. Cards contain multiline titles and several compact tag chips. A second collection view is visible behind this foreground screen.

screens.name: Document assistant conversation
screens.layout: The visible conversation header has a menu control, truncated title, compose icon, and close button. A user question is followed by an assistant response with linked document references. Another request appears above a folder attachment card, while the lower composer includes attachment and execution-mode controls.

screens.name: Rich note with callout and checklist
screens.layout: Back, information, and overflow controls frame the top of a note. A large title leads into prose containing an inline tag and emphasized text. A bordered callout sits between the introduction and a Print queue heading. The checklist below mixes checked and unchecked items before an image.

screens.name: Note formatting keyboard
screens.layout: The visible note contains collapsible headings, a two-column table, and a short paragraph with the text cursor. Beneath the content, an attachment strip provides camera and media controls. A dense formatting keyboard fills the lower area with heading, emphasis, list, link, checklist, and indentation controls.

screens.name: Note with diagram and formula
screens.layout: A title and introductory sentence appear below back, information, and overflow controls. The note then contains a branching flowchart centered in the page. An explanatory paragraph follows, with highlighted words and an inline variable, and a mathematical formula occupies its own line beneath the paragraph.

screens.name: Drawing embedded in note
screens.layout: The note header provides back, information, and overflow controls. A title introduces a short character description with an inline tag and emphasized words. A dotted drawing surface contains an illustration below the prose. A floating drawing toolbar presents several pen tools and a color selector along the bottom.

screens.name: Workspace switcher over note sidebar
screens.layout: A navigation sidebar fills most of the screen, while part of the note list remains visible at the right edge. The current workspace control is expanded into a menu containing a general Notes entry, a checked pinned workspace, and recent tags. Additional tag rows continue beneath the menu.

screens.name: Find inside a note
screens.layout: A note title sits above an illustration, an attached PDF card, and body text with a highlighted matching word. A table begins below the paragraph. A search panel overlays the bottom, containing the query field, clear control, match count, close control, and previous and next arrows.

screens.name: Locked notes list
screens.layout: The list header places a navigation icon on the left, a Locked selector in the center, and search on the right. A Lock All Notes control sits beneath it. Each separated note row retains a readable title and relative timestamp while its body preview appears as obscured blocks.

screens.name: Linked evergreen note
screens.layout: A compact top bar contains the sidebar control, truncated note name, reading icon, and overflow menu. The document begins with a large multiline heading and a tag chip. Paragraphs include underlined links and a bulleted link list. A bottom toolbar provides history, new-note, tab, and navigation controls.

screens.name: Trip checklist note
screens.layout: The page title and two tag chips precede a To-do section. Checkbox items include an indented group of people, where completed entries are struck through. An Ideas heading introduces nested bullets and linked destination names. The top bar holds note controls, and the bottom bar includes history and tabs.

screens.name: Markdown note editing
screens.layout: The trip-planning note retains its title, tags, and checkbox hierarchy above an open software keyboard. A visible destination uses bracketed link syntax. A horizontal editing accessory bar separates the document from the keyboard, with controls for checkboxes, attachments, headings, bold, italic, and strikethrough.

screens.name: Vault file drawer
screens.layout: The open Notes drawer shows file and folder counts beneath its heading, with a settings control at the right. A Files section contains collapsible folders and note rows. Projects is expanded and the current note is highlighted. New-note, new-folder, sorting, and collapse controls line the bottom.

screens.name: Backlinks drawer
screens.layout: A drawer overlays the right side of a note, beginning with the note name and word and character counts. The Backlinks heading has utility controls beside it. Linked mentions contains three expandable source rows with counts, followed by an Unlinked mentions heading and a bottom utility toolbar.

screens.name: Open note tabs sheet
screens.layout: A bottom sheet overlays a dimmed trip-planning note. Its first row is a New tab action with a plus icon. Three open note rows follow, each beginning with a document icon. A checkmark appears at the right of the currently selected trip-planning note.

screens.name: Journal entry list
screens.layout: A journal title occupies the upper section below back, search, overflow, and profile controls. A rounded content area starts with List, Calendar, Media, and Map tabs. Month headings organize entry rows with left-aligned dates, titles, excerpt text, metadata, and small media thumbnails at the right.

screens.name: Journal media gallery
screens.layout: Back, search, overflow, and profile controls sit above the journal view tabs, with Media selected. A second segmented row filters All, Photo, Video, Audio, and PDF. The body uses a two-column image grid with dates overlaid on thumbnails, and a circular add button floats near the lower right.

screens.name: Journal photo calendar
screens.layout: The Calendar tab is selected beneath the journal's top controls. Month sections stack vertically, each using a seven-column date grid. Some cells contain photographs while others show only a day number. Month labels divide the grids, and an add button floats over the lower-right corner.

screens.name: Shared journal information
screens.layout: The journal title and year range appear above view tabs, with the journal-information icon selected. The body has separate Members, Description, and Stats sections. Member avatars overlap in a small row. Statistic tiles vary in size, while Edit and a circular add control sit near the bottom.

screens.name: Journal template gallery
screens.layout: A centered Templates title and back control sit above Gallery and My Templates tabs. The Gallery view groups cards under Getting Started and Reflections, each with a short description. Large illustrated template cards run horizontally within each group, with labels such as Daily Gratitude, Morning, Evening, and Weekly.

screens.name: On This Day journal entry
screens.layout: A compact sheet header shows the On This Day count and date between overflow and confirmation controls. A map occupies the next section. Year group headings follow, with a past-year entry card containing a bold opening sentence, body text, and a photograph extending below the visible area.

screens.name: Printed journal book preview
screens.layout: A Close button sits above a book-production view. The upper row pairs a cover preview with a Cover label and Edit button. A second row pairs Content and another Edit button with a two-page spread preview. An estimated page count is centered near the bottom of the visible screen.

screens.name: Journal collection list
screens.layout: The Journals heading sits beneath a new-folder control, search, and profile avatar. The list begins with All Entries, then shows journals and expandable groups with colored book icons, names, and entry counts. Overflow controls appear beside several rows, with Trash and a New Journal button at the bottom.

screens.name: Journal home recommendations
screens.layout: A profile avatar appears above an On This Day section containing a horizontal set of memory cards and a See more link. Daily Prompt follows with another See more control and a large prompt card. An Add from Photo Library section begins below with Select and an image grid.

screens.name: Meditation exploration categories
screens.layout: A search field begins the visible app region. Four category tiles form a two-column grid below it, labeled Meditate, Sleep, Move, and Music. Additional topic cards continue underneath. A publisher-enlarged program card partially covers this lower list, leaving its title, level, duration, and instructor metadata readable.

screens.name: Sleep content categories
screens.layout: The visible app has a back button and centered Sleep heading above a vertical list of large content cards. Each card combines a title, a short explanation, and an illustration aligned toward the right. Wind Downs, Sleep Music, and Kids and Parents are visible above the three-item bottom navigation.

screens.name: Meditation course detail
screens.layout: The visible course detail begins with a back control over a large illustration. Below it, the Basics title has a favorite icon opposite. Course type and duration appear above a short description. A teacher-selection area is partly enlarged in the publisher frame, with named choices and a Begin Course button.

screens.name: Daily meditation schedule
screens.layout: A greeting leads the app view, with favorite, history, and notification icons beside it. Start your day introduces stacked activity cards aligned with a vertical dotted progress line. Each card contains a title, activity type, duration, and thumbnail. Today is selected in the bottom navigation.

screens.name: Meditation recommendation
screens.layout: A back control and Meditate heading sit above a large illustration. The recommendation area presents a course title, duration, and Play button. Below it, Recent and Recommended tabs precede a compact course row with thumbnail, title, metadata, and trailing chevron. The bottom bar has three navigation destinations.

screens.name: Sleep story browsing
screens.layout: The visible Sleep screen begins with a title and horizontally arranged filter chips, including Sleep Stories, All, Meditations, Tools, and Music. A Featured heading has a See All link opposite. Large portrait cover cards follow horizontally, with story titles and creator metadata underneath the artwork.

screens.name: Daily practice library
screens.layout: A Daily Practice heading is followed by a short introductory sentence. The main content is a two-column grid of large portrait cards. Each card pairs an image and program name with a text label below; the first row also shows short descriptions. More programs continue below the visible crop.

screens.name: Soundscape and music shelves
screens.layout: A Soundscapes heading has a See All link aligned to the right. Two large image cards sit side by side below it, with play symbols and labels. A divider separates this shelf from Soothing Music, which repeats the heading-and-link arrangement above another horizontal row of illustrated cards.

screens.name: Audio collection detail
screens.layout: Back and overflow controls overlay a large artwork area. The collection title appears below, with a favorite icon at the right. A curator row precedes side-by-side Play and Shuffle buttons. A short descriptive paragraph sits beneath these primary controls in the visible lower portion of the screen.

screens.name: Activity discussion
screens.layout: A back label and Discussion title sit above a small activity map. The activity title and author metadata precede a kudos count and overlapping avatars. Comments stack with avatars, names, timestamps, text, and like counts. A comment field with Send appears above the five-item bottom navigation.

screens.name: Sport selection sheet
screens.layout: A map with a recorded route occupies the upper part of the screen beneath Hide, Run, and settings controls. A bottom sheet begins with Choose a Sport. Circular icons form a Your Top Sports row, followed by a Foot Sports list where Run carries a selection checkmark.

screens.name: Weight training activity detail
screens.layout: A back button and overflow control frame a large front-and-back muscle illustration. A small media thumbnail sits below the figure. The lower panel shows the athlete, timestamp, activity title, and a two-column set of metrics for elapsed time, volume, sets, and heart rate above the bottom navigation.

screens.name: Social activity feed card
screens.layout: The Home header contains profile, search, messaging, and notification controls. An activity card begins with the athlete and timestamp, followed by a title and metric row. A large photograph dominates the center. Kudos avatars, comment count, reaction controls, and a comment appear below, above the bottom navigation.

screens.name: Activity progress comparison
screens.layout: The Progress header is followed by sport and metric filter chips. Two distance totals summarize the compared periods above a line chart with month labels and distance ticks. A comparison legend sits beneath the chart, then a short progress summary card. Five navigation items remain fixed at the bottom.

screens.name: Route discovery map
screens.layout: A map fills most of the screen behind a sport selector, search bar, bookmark control, and route-filter chips. A highlighted route crosses the map. Layer, 3D, location, and edit controls form a vertical rail. A route card with photograph and metrics sits above a route-count strip and bottom navigation.

screens.name: Segment leaderboard
screens.layout: A back label and Leaderboards title precede horizontal period and athlete filters. A featured record area shows an athlete image, time, and name above the rankings. The table aligns rank, athlete, and time or pace, with avatars and dates inside rows. Bottom navigation remains visible beneath the results.

screens.name: Trail discovery feed
screens.layout: A search field and filter control sit above horizontal category chips. Large trail cards stack below, combining landscape photographs, bookmark controls, names, locations, ratings, difficulty, distance, and estimated time. A floating Map button overlays the lower card, while five navigation destinations line the bottom edge.

screens.name: Trail detail summary
screens.layout: A large trail photograph holds back, share, status, and bookmark controls, plus pagination dots and a play button. A rounded panel overlaps its lower edge with the trail title and rating. Four metrics form a two-column grid, followed by descriptive text and paired Download and Map buttons.

screens.name: Trail photo tour
screens.layout: A full-height landscape photograph sits behind close, share, and gallery controls. A bottom panel shows current distance and elevation beside a pause button, with an elevation profile beneath. Tabs along the panel's bottom edge include Latest, Sights, Seasons, and the selected Tour state.

screens.name: Trail weather overlay
screens.layout: A route and weather overlay fill the upper map, with layer, 3D, compass, and location controls along the right. A precipitation legend sits above a bottom sheet. The sheet presents a percentage, location metrics, and a precipitation profile, followed by a day selector, time, and horizontal slider.

screens.name: Offline trail download area
screens.layout: A map displays numbered trail clusters and individual trail markers within a rectangular outlined download area. A circular close control sits inside the upper-left corner. A prominent Download 104 trails button is centered near the bottom of the selection rectangle, with the app's five-item navigation bar below.

screens.name: Three-dimensional trail preview
screens.layout: A tilted terrain map occupies the full screen, with a trail line and current position marker over the landscape. A close control is in the upper-left corner, while length and elevation gain appear in a compact box opposite. A bottom card names the trail and includes a pause control.

screens.name: Trail reviews with photos
screens.layout: Reviews stack vertically with a divider between them. Each begins with an avatar, reviewer name, star rating, relative date, and overflow control. The first includes labeled conditions before its body text, a horizontal photo strip, and a View activity link. The next review repeats the author and image structure.

screens.name: Paused trail navigation
screens.layout: The map shows the route and a directional position marker, with collapse, layer, compass, and location controls. A rounded bottom sheet contains six metrics arranged in two rows. An elevation profile follows with a current-position marker, above large Resume and Finish buttons along the sheet's lower edge.

screens.name: Weekly running activity
screens.layout: An avatar and add control sit above the Activity heading. A segmented period selector precedes a This Week dropdown and large distance total. Runs, average pace, and time appear in a metric row above a weekday bar chart. Recent Activity begins below, immediately above the bottom navigation.

screens.name: Guided run start screen
screens.layout: Bookmark and close controls occupy the upper corners of a full-screen guided-run artwork. A large centered run title appears above a short distance and activity label. Near the bottom, a prominent circular Start button sits between smaller settings and music controls, all over the artwork.

screens.name: Training plan card
screens.layout: A profile avatar sits above the Plans heading and divider. A large plan card begins with prominent cover artwork and the plan name. Below the image, a duration label leads into a short descriptive paragraph. A small Beginner tag appears near the bottom of the visible card.

screens.name: Training plan overview
screens.layout: A coach photograph fills the upper portion beneath back and share controls. The plan distance and a Plan Overview play button overlay the image near its bottom. A lower panel lists duration, weekly frequency, run types, and suitability with leading icons, followed by another Plan Overview heading.

screens.name: Community running challenge
screens.layout: A large photograph occupies the top of the visible challenge card. The content panel below starts with the time remaining until the challenge begins. A multiline challenge title follows, then several lines of explanatory text. The visible crop ends mid-description without showing a join control.

screens.name: Shoe mileage milestone
screens.layout: A close button appears in the upper-right corner of the milestone screen. A large mileage figure sits above a shoe image in the center, with small celebratory marks around it. Below, a large congratulations heading precedes a brief message describing the mileage goal reached on these shoes.

screens.name: Course selection list
screens.layout: A close control and centered Courses heading sit above a vertically divided list. Each course row contains a flag or subject icon, a bold name, and a trailing chevron. Language courses and subjects such as Chess, Math, and Music share the same row structure in the visible app area.

screens.name: Vocabulary image question
screens.layout: A close control, progress bar, and energy count form the top row. The question heading appears above an audio button and a word in Chinese characters. Four illustrated answer cards are arranged in a two-column grid, each with a label; the milk card is visibly selected.

screens.name: Chess puzzle lesson
screens.layout: The lesson header contains close, progress, and energy indicators. A Solve the puzzle heading precedes a character and speech bubble describing the move objective. The board fills the remaining app region, showing pieces, a selected piece ring, and an arrow toward a target square.

screens.name: Sentence translation exercise
screens.layout: A lesson progress bar and energy count sit above the translation prompt. A character's speech bubble contains an audio control and source sentence. Selected word tiles form the answer on ruled lines. Below, unused words and empty placeholders occupy a separate word bank in the visible exercise area.

screens.name: Interactive conversation scene
screens.layout: An illustrated café scene fills the app region, with characters positioned around tables and a counter. A dialogue card overlays the center, labeled with the speaker's name and an audio icon beside the French text. A circular arrow control appears beside the dialogue near the lower-right corner.

screens.name: Daily streak result
screens.layout: A character illustration and speech bubble appear above a very large streak count. The day streak label sits directly beneath the number. A rounded weekly strip follows, showing weekday initials and completion circles, with the first three days checked and the remaining days unfilled in the visible state.

screens.name: Number construction exercise
screens.layout: Close, progress, and energy controls appear above a Create this number heading. A large target number is centered below. The answer area uses a row of filled and dashed slots, while number and operator tiles are arranged beneath it. One multiplication tile is visibly offset above the remaining choices.

screens.name: Speaking exercise prompt
screens.layout: The lesson view has backward and forward arrows above a short progress line. A Listen, then say it out loud instruction precedes a photograph. The phrase appears in an audio row, enlarged by the publisher, with an English translation beneath it and a large circular microphone control at the bottom.

screens.name: Language learning plan
screens.layout: A greeting and profile control head the screen, with Today and Learning Plan tabs below. An expanded topic groups lesson rows. Each combines an illustrated lesson tile, a brief objective, and a trailing action. The completed first lesson offers Repeat, while subsequent lessons show Start now and Start.

screens.name: Listen and repeat dialogue
screens.layout: Lesson navigation arrows, a close control, and a progress line sit above the Listen and repeat instruction. Alternating dialogue bubbles show Spanish lines with English translations and small character avatars. The selected phrase is repeated in an audio panel below, followed by its translation and a large microphone button.

screens.name: Learning exploration catalog
screens.layout: An Explore heading and profile control appear at the top of the visible app. Large cards follow for a live speaking option and Audio Recap, each containing a title, description, and illustration. A Games heading introduces another card below, partly cut off by the publisher frame.

screens.name: Review method selector
screens.layout: A centered question asks how the learner would like to review, with a close button to its right. Large rounded rows stack below for Listening, Speaking, Flashcards, Games, and Writing. Each pairs a leading method icon with a bold label and trailing chevron; the publisher enlarges the Speaking row.

screens.name: Learning reminder schedule
screens.layout: A back button, Set reminders heading, and close control form the top bar. Introductory text precedes seven weekday buttons. The Choose times section includes a Same time for selected days toggle, then selected weekdays in a vertical list with individual time buttons aligned to the right.

screens.name: Podcast playback
screens.layout: Podcast artwork is centered high on the screen with ample surrounding space. Beneath it, a progress slider shows elapsed and remaining time. Previous, skip-back, pause, skip-forward, and next controls form a horizontal row. Three playback-speed choices appear below the main transport controls.

screens.name: Airbnb discovery home
screens.layout: A rounded search field sits above three illustrated tabs for Homes, Experiences, and Services. Below, a Recently viewed homes carousel precedes a second destination section. Each compact property card combines a photo, favorite heart, location label, and a short price or rating line.

screens.name: Airbnb home search results
screens.layout: A back arrow and filter icon flank the destination and guest summary at the top. Large property photographs lead vertically stacked results, with favorite hearts and image pagination dots overlaid. Beneath each photograph, the listing title, rating, description, cancellation text, and price form a compact text block.

screens.name: Airbnb experience results
screens.layout: The destination summary appears between a back arrow and filter control, followed by Type and Duration chips. Experience results use a four-image collage above the title, activity type, duration, starting price, and review summary. Favorite hearts sit over the upper corner of each collage.

screens.name: Airbnb service discovery
screens.layout: A location and service summary anchors the top toolbar. A horizontal row of service categories pairs square thumbnails with names and availability counts. The Chefs section below uses large food photographs, an overlaid favorite control and popularity badge, followed by the provider title and per-guest price.

screens.name: Airbnb host conversation
screens.layout: The conversation header centers the host avatar and name between a back arrow and Details button, with a trip summary beneath. Incoming text and a large video attachment occupy the left side, including a playback triangle and reactions. A short outgoing reply sits separately on the right.

screens.name: Airbnb trip itinerary
screens.layout: The Trips heading and destination sit above a reservation card containing a large property photo, title, dates, host, address, and Get directions button. Below the card, a dated vertical itinerary aligns a day marker with separate activity rows containing thumbnails, event names, and times.

screens.name: Airbnb host type selection
screens.layout: A close control appears above the question asking what the user would like to host. Three large stacked choices are labeled Home, Experience, and Service. Each card aligns its label on the left and an illustrative icon on the right, with the first choice visibly outlined.

screens.name: Booking travel search
screens.layout: The search form stacks destination, date range, and occupancy fields above a full-width Search button. Below, a Deals heading introduces a horizontal strip of destination photographs with city names and date ranges beneath each image. The app branding occupies the header above the form.

screens.name: Booking accommodation results
screens.layout: A destination search box sits above a three-part toolbar for Sort, Filter, and Map. Property results combine left-side thumbnails with hotel names, star classifications, review-score badges, and supporting location or cleanliness text. Favorite hearts occupy the upper right of individual listing rows.

screens.name: Booking hotel detail
screens.layout: The toolbar provides a back arrow beside the hotel name. A large property photograph occupies the upper content area. The hotel summary groups its name, star classification, address, a mobile-price label, and the original and current prices above a wide Select room button.

screens.name: Booking trip reservations
screens.layout: A destination heading introduces a vertical sequence of reservation cards. Each card pairs a transport or property thumbnail with a booking title and short status line, and places an overflow control at the right edge. A faint vertical connector links the cards into a trip sequence.

screens.name: TripIt upcoming trips
screens.layout: The Trips heading appears above a search field for places, dates, and travel plans. Trip rows pair destination photographs with a trip name, date range, duration, and a countdown until departure. An overflow control is visible in the upper right above the list.

screens.name: TripIt expanded flight alert
screens.layout: An expanded notification displays a flight identifier and delay summary above a compact departure-and-arrival card. The card places airport times side by side with terminal and gate details underneath. A separate action menu below offers Call Your Travel Agency, Search For Alternate Flights, and View Details.

screens.name: TripIt flight itinerary detail
screens.layout: The flight route title is followed by airline and confirmation information. A vertical journey line connects departure and arrival locations, times, and map links, with duration and seat information between them. A disabled check-in control appears above a Documents section containing a document thumbnail and add tile.

screens.name: TripIt destination information
screens.layout: A centered destination title sits above a country-information row with a chevron. Under an Overview label, stacked topic cards show COVID-19 status, vaccination, and testing information. Each card pairs an icon with a topic heading, brief supporting text, and a small Learn More link near the lower edge.

screens.name: TripIt nearby cafes
screens.layout: A toolbar labeled Nearby Cafes sits over a street map marked with numerous circular locations and a highlighted hotel. The lower portion contains cafe rows with names, distances, ratings, opening status, and trailing chevrons. A five-item navigation bar remains visible beneath the list.

screens.name: TripIt airport departure countdown
screens.layout: The Go Now title sits above a flight-departure strip and two settings rows: an alert toggle and an airport arrival lead-time value. A large circular countdown dominates the lower area, showing hours, minutes, and seconds beneath a suggested departure time and a short location-and-traffic note.

screens.name: TripIt flight carbon footprint
screens.layout: The flight-specific title and route sit above a prominent carbon total and a short household-energy comparison. An illustration separates this summary from two suggested-action chips. A Take Action section below includes a thumbnail, explanatory text, and Learn more link above the persistent bottom navigation.

screens.name: TripIt travel statistics
screens.layout: A Travel Stats toolbar includes back and share controls. A horizontal year selector precedes a prominent total distance and explanatory comparison. Four divided rows list days, trips, countries or regions, and cities with small icons on the left and numeric totals aligned at the right.

screens.name: Flighty flight overview
screens.layout: A globe with several connecting flight paths occupies the upper portion. A rounded My Flights panel overlaps its lower edge, with share and profile controls beside the title. Flight rows show airline identifiers, routes, current status, airport codes, and times, with bottom navigation below the list.

screens.name: Flighty incoming aircraft
screens.layout: A satellite map with weather imagery and an aircraft marker fills the upper area. A rounded Where’s My Plane panel overlaps the map and presents aircraft type, registration, age, and an airplane illustration. A delay warning and vertically arranged flight-status details continue underneath the aircraft summary.

screens.name: Flighty friends flights
screens.layout: A map with flight paths and profile markers sits above a rounded Friends’ Flights panel. The panel header includes a dropdown, sharing control, and avatar. A search field and horizontal person filters precede flight rows pairing profile icons with route names, landing countdowns, airport codes, and times.

screens.name: Flighty live flight detail
screens.layout: A map with aircraft markers fills the upper screen. A rounded flight panel shows the airline, date, route, and close control, followed by a status explanation. Departure and arrival sections emphasize times beside gate badges, with terminals and timing notes underneath; action controls run along the bottom.

screens.name: Flighty flight passport
screens.layout: The Flighty Passport title is flanked by close and share controls above a horizontal year selector. A world map displays connected routes with a strip of country flags below. A passport summary groups the flight count and distance as large figures, with flight time and destination totals beneath.

screens.name: Revolut savings account
screens.layout: The account name and large balance are centered over a background image, with an Accounts button underneath. Four circular actions sit in a row above a transaction panel showing estimated interest and a savings transfer. A See all link and smaller monthly summary cards appear below the activity.

screens.name: Revolut security settings
screens.layout: A Security heading sits above three circular shortcuts for reporting fraud, a lost card, and a lost device. A separate wealth-protection card precedes grouped navigation rows for card security, card connections, payments, and payees. Additional sign-in and device settings continue below with trailing chevrons.

screens.name: Revolut joint account activity
screens.layout: The joint-account label and prominent balance sit over a photograph above an Accounts control. Add money, Move, Details, and More actions form an evenly spaced row. A grouped activity panel beneath lists an upcoming payment and recent named expenses, with amounts aligned right and a See all link below.

screens.name: Revolut investment account
screens.layout: A capital-at-risk label precedes the large account balance and Accounts button. Four circular actions for Trade, Add money, Withdraw, and More divide the summary from a holdings panel. That panel begins with an account total and percentage change, followed by individual fund rows with distinctive icons.

screens.name: Revolut payment conversation
screens.layout: The header centers the recipient’s name and handle between back and profile controls. Alternating message bubbles include payment cards with amounts, descriptions, timestamps, and one attached photo. Request and Send buttons sit above the message composer, combining the transaction thread and text-entry controls on one screen.

screens.name: Revolut account automations
screens.layout: The account balance and Accounts control occupy the upper image area. A row of Add money, Move, Details, and More buttons separates the summary from an Automations panel. Three chevron rows show a recurring transfer, income sorting, and spare change, each with an icon and supporting schedule or status text.

screens.name: Revolut cryptocurrency holdings
screens.layout: A large portfolio balance and small change indicator appear above a compact line chart. Trade, Receive, Send, and More actions form a row beneath it. The holdings panel lists individual assets using icons, names, quantities, and reference prices on the left, with values and percentage changes aligned right.

screens.name: Wise currency account
screens.layout: A centered balance and Account details button sit above circular Add, Convert, Send, and Request actions. A segmented control switches among Currencies, Transactions, and Options. The visible currency list begins with Add a currency and continues with flag-marked balances, while four main navigation items remain at the bottom.

screens.name: Wise transfer amount
screens.layout: Two amount rows dominate the panel, each pairing a currency selector with a large numeric value for the sender and recipient. A guarantee badge sits at the top. Arrival speed and total fees appear as separate supporting rows before a full-width Send money button at the bottom.

screens.name: Wise currency selection
screens.layout: A back arrow sits above the Choose a currency heading and a rounded search field. Under Your currencies, a single-column list pairs country flags with currency codes. The rows are widely spaced, and the visible selection area extends through several currencies without additional card containers.

screens.name: Wise transfer review
screens.layout: The upper form pairs sender and recipient currencies with large amounts. Beneath it, separate rows show the payment card, expected arrival, and total fees, with Change and Schedule controls aligned to the right. A small reassurance line sits immediately above the full-width Continue button at the bottom.

screens.name: Wise card management
screens.layout: The Cards heading and Order a card button sit above a large physical-card preview and masked card number. Three circular actions provide Show PIN, Card details, and Freeze card. A Manage card section contains a payment-methods row with a chevron, followed by four-item bottom navigation.

screens.name: Monzo account home
screens.layout: A top utility row contains profile, Upgrade, gift, search, and add controls. The account card emphasizes the balance and provides Add money and Card actions. The Activity list below mixes upcoming payments with individual transactions, using merchant icons and supporting notes on the left and amounts on the right.

screens.name: Monzo privacy and security
screens.layout: A back arrow accompanies the Privacy & security title. The first section shows a current call-status card with a profile image and information icon. A profile-privacy row follows, then two separate Face ID settings with switches aligned on the right for authentication and unlocking the app.

screens.name: Monzo savings pot
screens.layout: The Savings title is flanked by close and settings controls. A named pot image, prominent balance, and Withdraw and Add money buttons form the main summary. A savings-goal panel with progress bar appears above an Activity list showing interest and personal-account transfers with right-aligned amounts.

screens.name: Monzo credit account
screens.layout: A back control sits above a credit-account card displaying the balance, available credit, and payment due information. Pay now and Card controls appear within that card. The Payments section lists Pay early and Pay extra options, followed by upcoming-payment text and an Activity list of merchant purchases.

screens.name: YNAB budget home
screens.layout: The Home heading sits above two horizontal status rows for new transactions and money ready to assign, each with a matching action button. A Top Priorities section follows with named budget categories and right-aligned available amounts. An August Summary section begins beneath the priority list.

screens.name: YNAB plan targets
screens.layout: A back control appears above Edit Plan and a prominent Cost to Be Me total. A targets summary compares the month’s target amount with monthly income using horizontal bars. Category groups below contain named targets, contribution amounts, due-date text, overflow controls, and Add Target actions.

screens.name: YNAB monthly budget
screens.layout: The toolbar centers the selected month between menu, editing, and overflow controls. A Ready to Assign banner sits above grouped budget categories. Each group has a collapsible heading; category rows align names and available amounts, with progress bars and short funded or spent status messages beneath.

screens.name: YNAB savings category detail
screens.layout: A completion control appears at the upper right above the named vacation category. The Balance section lists prior-month funds, assigned money, activity, and available funds in aligned rows. A Target section below presents a large success symbol, a completion message, and the target amount and date.

screens.name: YNAB cover overspending
screens.layout: The Cover Overspending sheet presents the overspent category and negative amount above a Select Category control. A second sheet rises from below with a search field and grouped source categories. Each selectable row pairs a category name and icon with its available balance at the right.

screens.name: YNAB shared plan members
screens.layout: The YNAB Together sheet includes a close control, illustration, and short sharing explanation. Separate Group Manager and Members headings organize the people list. Each rounded row contains a name and email address on the left with a chevron on the right, distinguishing the owner from other members.

screens.name: YNAB financial reflection
screens.layout: A Reflect header and overflow control sit above stacked analytical cards. The first card includes a short income-versus-spending statement, grouped monthly bars, labeled axes, and a legend. The Net Worth card beneath emphasizes a total, lists assets and debts, and begins a combined bar-and-line chart.

screens.name: YNAB learning and support
screens.layout: The Home toolbar sits above a month row and a short learning link. A For You heading with See More precedes a large illustrated reading card containing a title and reading duration. A support prompt and prominent Connect With Our Team button appear beneath the recommended content.

screens.name: Copilot money dashboard
screens.layout: The Copilot header sits over a horizontal section selector with Dashboard selected. A budget card emphasizes the remaining amount above a small trend line. A To Review section contains suggested transaction corrections, merchant rows, and Dismiss and Approve All controls; the next budget section begins below.

screens.name: Copilot budget setup
screens.layout: The Your budget toolbar appears above an explanatory callout. A compact table groups spending categories and subcategories, aligning average spending and proposed budgets in separate numeric columns. The lower summary emphasizes a total monthly budget above a comparison bar with average spending and income labels underneath.

screens.name: Copilot cash flow
screens.layout: The Copilot header and horizontal section navigation place Cash flow in the selected position. A Net income card presents a date range, total, percentage change, and comparison text above monthly bars. A Spend card below repeats that hierarchy and begins a stacked spending chart.

screens.name: Copilot investment overview
screens.layout: The selected Investments section shows a portfolio total and change above a large line chart with time-range controls. A horizontally arranged movers section places ticker names, miniature charts, and percentage changes in compact cards. The Accounts list below pairs institution icons and account names with balances and changes.

screens.name: Copilot money assistant conversation
screens.layout: A user question appears in a right-aligned bubble above an analysis-status line and assistant response. The reply includes a Retirement Savings card with a five-year stacked bar chart and legend. Feedback icons sit beneath the answer, while an Ask Copilot composer and send control anchor the bottom.

screens.name: Copilot recurring payments
screens.layout: The Recurrings tab is selected beneath the Copilot header. A summary card pairs a circular progress indicator with the amount paid so far. This Month presents recurring expenses as a compact card grid with icons, amounts, dates, and checkmarks, followed by an In the Future section below.

screens.name: Spotify listening home
screens.layout: A profile avatar precedes filter chips for All, Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks. A two-column block of compact shortcuts pairs cover thumbnails with playlist or show names. Below, a Jump back in section begins a row of larger cover cards, creating two levels of content navigation.

screens.name: Spotify video podcast player
screens.layout: The player header contains a collapse arrow, show name, and overflow control. A large video area sits above a Switch to audio button and episode information. A progress slider includes elapsed and remaining times, with speed, skip-back, pause, and skip-forward controls arranged underneath.

screens.name: Spotify editorial playlist
screens.layout: Large cover artwork leads into the playlist title, description, publisher, save count, and duration. An action row includes add, download, overflow, shuffle, and play controls. Track rows pair artwork with song and artist names and trailing menus; a compact current-track player spans the bottom.

screens.name: Spotify shared blend playlist
screens.layout: The playlist artwork appears above a two-person title, description, publisher, save count, and total duration. An action row includes saved, download, collaborator, overflow, shuffle, and play controls. Track rows add small participant avatars beside song metadata, and a compact now-playing strip remains below the list.

screens.name: Spotify audiobook discovery
screens.layout: A profile avatar, close control, and Audiobooks chip appear above stacked recommendation cards. Each card places the book title and author above centered cover art, followed by publication and duration information, descriptive text, and a preview button. Add, overflow, and play controls sit within each card.

screens.name: Spotify search and browse
screens.layout: A profile avatar and camera control flank the Search heading above a prominent query field. Start browsing uses a two-column category grid. Explore your genres introduces narrower image tiles in a horizontal row, while a Browse all section begins another set of category cards underneath.

screens.name: Spotify library
screens.layout: The Your Library toolbar contains profile, search, and add controls. A horizontal row of content-type chips precedes a Recents sorting row and view-toggle icon. Saved items appear as vertically stacked rows with cover art, names, type or creator metadata, and occasional pinned or update indicators.

screens.name: Spotify personal playlist
screens.layout: A four-image cover collage appears above the playlist title, owner, and duration. The action row includes download, collaborators, overflow, shuffle, and play controls. An Add to this playlist row precedes individual tracks with artwork, titles, artists, and menus, while a persistent mini-player occupies the bottom.

screens.name: Pocket Casts now playing
screens.layout: A top strip offers Now Playing, Details, and a partially visible bookmarks tab. Large podcast artwork dominates the center above the episode title and show name. A progress slider separates this metadata from large skip-back, pause, and skip-forward controls, with smaller playback tools arranged below.

screens.name: Pocket Casts podcast library
screens.layout: The Podcasts toolbar places a folder-add control opposite an overflow menu. A search field spans the width above a three-column grid of show covers, including one folder-style tile. A compact playback bar sits just above the five-item bottom navigation for podcasts, playlists, discovery, queue, and profile.

screens.name: Pocket Casts favorites playlist
screens.layout: A cover collage and Favorites title sit above the episode count and total duration. Smart rules and Play all buttons precede a search field. Episode rows combine cover art, dates, titles, durations, and trailing play controls, while a mini-player and main navigation remain along the bottom.

screens.name: Pocket Casts playback queue
screens.layout: The Up Next toolbar is flanked by Clear and Select buttons. A current-episode row appears above total remaining time and a shuffle control. Queued episodes show cover thumbnails, publication dates, titles, durations, and drag handles. A mini-player and bottom navigation sit beneath the queue.

screens.name: Pocket Casts playback effects
screens.layout: A Playback Effects sheet overlays the lower half of the now-playing screen. A segmented control distinguishes all podcasts from the current podcast. Speed uses minus, value, and plus controls, followed by Trim Silence and Volume Boost switches with explanatory text and a saved-time summary beneath the silence setting.

screens.name: Overcast podcast home
screens.layout: The header centers Overcast between settings and search icons. Compact recent-episode cards form two horizontal rows above a Playlists section of circular shortcuts. The Podcasts section includes a Current/All segmented control, then show rows with cover art, title, creator text, and trailing chevrons.

screens.name: Letterboxd film detail
screens.layout: A large film backdrop fills the upper area with back and overflow controls overlaid. The film title, release year, director, trailer control, and runtime sit beneath it alongside a small poster. A tagline and synopsis lead into a ratings section with a distribution chart and average rating.

screens.name: Letterboxd film actions
screens.layout: The film title and year sit in a centered header opposite a close control. A large poster occupies most of the visible screen. Along its lower edge, a row of distinct action icons represents watched status, liking, rating, and adding the film to a list or collection.

screens.name: Letterboxd viewing diary
screens.layout: The toolbar centers the owner’s diary title with a back link on the left. A month-and-year heading groups a vertical film log. Each row begins with the calendar day and a small poster, followed by the film title, release year, star rating, and occasional heart or repeat-viewing icon.

screens.name: Letterboxd film review
screens.layout: The Review toolbar provides a back link and overflow menu. A reviewer avatar, name, and membership badge lead the content, with a small film poster aligned right. Film title, year, star rating, heart, and watched date precede a long review displayed as readable paragraphs across the remaining width.

screens.name: Letterboxd curated film list
screens.layout: The List toolbar includes a back link and sharing control. Creator identity and a membership badge appear above the list title and descriptive paragraph. A four-column poster grid follows, with small numbered badges attached to each poster to communicate the order of films in the collection.

screens.name: Letterboxd streaming services
screens.layout: The Service toolbar contains a Browse back link. My Services groups three navigation rows for purchase, rental, and streaming combinations. A By Service section lists providers with recognizable service icons and trailing chevrons. A data-provider attribution appears underneath the final visible service row.

screens.name: Letterboxd poster selection
screens.layout: The Change Poster toolbar places Cancel on the left and Save on the right. A compact source-tab row sits below, with Popular selected beside other providers. A two-column gallery fills the remaining area with alternative film posters, keeping each artwork inside similarly sized rectangular cells.

screens.name: Pinterest visual style results
screens.layout: A close control overlays a large source image, which also contains small attribute labels and a larger style phrase. A rounded results sheet rises over the lower part of the image. Its two-column masonry arrangement shows related visual items with image-led cards and small overflow controls.

screens.name: Pinterest similar products
screens.layout: A source photograph occupies the upper area, with a row of descriptive query chips across its lower edge. A rounded Shop similar sheet begins underneath. Product cards are arranged horizontally, each pairing a large square image with a short product name and price on separate lines.

screens.name: Pinterest skin tone filter
screens.layout: A Pick a skin tone range panel overlays a masonry search-results grid and presents four adjacent swatch choices, with one outlined as selected. Behind it, image cards vary in height and include labels or overflow menus. A bottom bar contains home, search-query, visual-search, and profile controls.

screens.name: Pinterest recipe pin detail
screens.layout: A large recipe photograph leads the page with a visual-search control overlaid near its lower corner. Below it, a horizontal action row shows likes, comments, share, overflow, and Save. Creator identity, recipe title, rating, duration, servings, See more, and a wide Visit site button follow.

screens.name: Pinterest group conversation
screens.layout: The header combines a back arrow, group avatar, group name, member count, and overflow menu. A board preview sits above a shared image and alternating message bubbles. A later activity entry shows several pin thumbnails, while the bottom composer includes attachment, text-entry, and heart controls.

screens.name: Are.na channel collection
screens.layout: A breadcrumb identifies the channel owner and title above a metadata block with creation time, modification time, item count, and followers. A description precedes Connect, Edit, search, and overflow controls. The collection below combines images and text blocks in two columns, with navigation icons along the bottom.

screens.name: Are.na profile channels
screens.layout: A breadcrumb-style profile heading is followed by a short biography and join date, with Follow, search, and overflow controls aligned nearby. Channels and Blocks tabs divide the content. Channel cards show titles, creator names, thumbnail strips, block counts, and update times above the persistent bottom navigation.

screens.name: Are.na create block
screens.layout: A large text-entry area is active above the on-screen keyboard. A compact menu at the upper right offers Text, Images, Camera, Files, Record, and Channel options with icons. Cancel and Next buttons sit side by side immediately above the keyboard, framing the content-entry step.

screens.name: Are.na channel mosaic
screens.layout: A channel-identification panel overlays the upper portion of an edge-to-edge mosaic. Follow, Connect, search, and overflow controls appear directly beneath its owner and title. The content forms a dense three-column grid that mixes image blocks and text excerpts, with a navigation strip across the bottom.

screens.name: Readwise Reader home collections
screens.layout: The Home heading appears above several named content sections, including Continue reading, Growth, and Shortlist. Each section contains horizontally arranged cards with cover images and title text, with author information visible under some cards. A row of compact navigation icons spans the lower edge of the screen.

screens.name: Readwise Reader highlight annotation
screens.layout: A long passage is displayed in a reading view with several consecutive lines highlighted. A lower annotation panel contains comment and tag controls, a Done action at the right, and a text note beneath. The selected passage remains visible above the panel as the focus of the screen.

screens.name: Readwise Reader assistant actions
screens.layout: A reading page with an article heading and body text remains visible behind a bottom sheet titled Ghostreader. The sheet places Cancel on the right and stacks command rows including Simplify, Summarize, and TL;DR. The commands occupy a separate panel over the lower portion of the article.

screens.name: Readwise Reader inbox swipe action
screens.layout: The Inbox header places search and overflow controls at the upper right. Article rows include source names, titles, excerpts, author or reading-time metadata, and thumbnails. One row is shifted sideways to reveal a large Later action with a clock icon, while neighboring rows remain in their normal positions.

screens.name: Reader views navigation
screens.layout: A Views heading sits above grouped navigation rows. Tags and Feeds form the first group; Articles, Books, Emails, PDFs, Tweets, Favorites, and a named collection follow below. Every row pairs a leading icon with a trailing chevron, while an overflow control sits above the heading.

screens.name: Instapaper saved articles
screens.layout: The Home toolbar places a back control on the left and search and overflow controls on the right. A vertical article list shows titles, source domains, reading durations, and excerpts. Compact thumbnails align along the right edge, and one article carries a notes badge beneath its excerpt.

screens.name: Instapaper save confirmation
screens.layout: A rounded sheet fills most of the display beneath a drag handle. The Instapaper mark and Saved status occupy the center with generous surrounding space. Three evenly spaced circular actions near the bottom are labeled Tag, Move, and Archive, each pairing a small icon with its caption.

screens.name: Instapaper article reader
screens.layout: An article title leads into author, publisher, and date metadata, followed by a large illustration and a continuous text column. A floating toolbar overlays the lower article area with back, favorite, archive, text appearance, and overflow controls. The body continues behind the toolbar toward the screen edge.

screens.name: Instapaper highlights and note
screens.layout: The reading column contains several highlighted passages within continuous prose. A small note marker sits beside a highlighted section, and a rounded annotation bubble overlays the following paragraph. The lower toolbar retains back, favorite, archive, text appearance, and overflow controls beneath the annotated content.

screens.name: Instapaper audio article player
screens.layout: A large article illustration sits above the article title and an overflow button. A central pause button is flanked by backward and forward fifteen-second controls. Below, a progress slider shows elapsed and remaining time, followed by a secondary row containing queue, audio, share, and playback-speed controls.

screens.name: 1Password login detail
screens.layout: A vault breadcrumb appears above an item icon and Amazon title. The detail body stacks labeled username, masked password, two-factor code, website, notes, and tags fields. Password strength appears beside the masked value, while the tag area includes a shopping label and a small plus control.

screens.name: 1Password password generator
screens.layout: An Editing toolbar provides Cancel and Save above the login item's name and credential fields. A password-generation panel occupies the lower screen with its own Cancel, refresh, and Use controls. A type selector, character-length slider, and separate Numbers and Symbols switches form the visible configuration area.

screens.name: 1Password share link options
screens.layout: A sharing sheet has a centered title, close control, and item identity near the top. Stacked rows show link expiration and audience selection, followed by an email chip and add-email control. A one-time-view switch and explanatory text precede Copy Link and a full-width Share Link button.

screens.name: 1Password Watchtower overview
screens.layout: The Watchtower heading sits below a profile image and opposite a circular add button. A large semicircular score gauge dominates the upper content, with a numeric score and rating inside it. A Share My Score control and explanatory paragraph appear above the start of an Overall Password Strength section and bottom navigation.

screens.name: Bitwarden vault
screens.layout: My vault appears above a search field and a grouped Types section showing credential categories with counts. A second group lists individual accounts with service icons, email subtitles, and overflow controls. A floating add button overlaps the list above a four-item navigation bar for vault, sending, generation, and settings.

screens.name: Bitwarden password generator
screens.layout: The Generator heading and profile control sit above Password, Passphrase, and Username tabs. A generated value with refresh control precedes a full-width Copy button. Length uses a slider; character classes use switches; minimum counts use minus and plus controls. The Generator destination is selected in the bottom navigation.

screens.name: Bitwarden text send editor
screens.layout: A New text send sheet places dismissal and confirmation controls at opposite corners. Name and Text fields lead into a hide-text switch. An expanded Additional options section contains deletion and expiration date rows with chevrons, explanatory copy, and a maximum-access count controlled by minus and plus buttons.

screens.name: Bitwarden vault unlock
screens.layout: The vault-unlock screen places an account avatar at upper left and an overflow menu at upper right. A master-password entry area includes a visibility icon, followed by explanatory text and the signed-in account. A wide Unlock button sits below these fields, leaving the lower screen largely empty.

screens.name: Proton Mail inbox
screens.layout: An Inbox toolbar contains a menu button, search icon, and account avatar, followed by an unread-count chip. Message rows pair sender icons with sender names, subject previews, and optional category labels or attachment chips. Timestamps and star controls align along the right side of the list.

screens.name: Proton Mail message composer
screens.layout: A compose sheet places close, scheduling, and Send controls across its top. Recipient, sender, and subject occupy separate labeled rows above the body text. The visible draft begins with a greeting and paragraph, while the on-screen keyboard occupies the lower portion beneath the message area.

screens.name: Proton Mail inbox swipe actions
screens.layout: The Inbox heading and account control sit above an unread-count chip and stacked message rows. Two rows are horizontally displaced, revealing an envelope action on the left and a trash action on the right. Remaining rows retain sender icons, subject previews, category labels, timestamps, and trailing star controls.

screens.name: Proton Calendar month and agenda
screens.layout: A month heading is centered between a menu control and date and add icons. The month grid uses weekday labels, date numbers, and small event dots, with one date selected. Beneath a divider and drag handle, the selected day's agenda begins with an all-day event followed by timed entries.

screens.name: Proton Calendar calendar drawer
screens.layout: An account card heads a navigation drawer that covers most of the calendar. My calendars and Subscribed calendars divide the list into groups. Each calendar has a square selection indicator beside its name, while a More section begins with Settings. A narrow strip of the underlying month remains visible on the right.

screens.name: Proton Calendar event detail
screens.layout: An event detail sheet places close, edit, and overflow controls along its top edge. The title is followed by the weekday, full date, and time range. A location row beneath contains a location icon, venue name, street address, and a trailing search icon aligned with the address block.

screens.name: Signal conversation list
screens.layout: The Chats toolbar combines an account image with camera and compose controls. A search field precedes Pinned and Chats groups. Conversation rows use circular avatars, names, snippets, and right-aligned times; some include unread badges. Chats, Calls, and Stories destinations appear in a bottom navigation bar.

screens.name: Signal disappearing-message conversation
screens.layout: The conversation header contains back, participant identity, and video and telephone controls. Alternating message bubbles include text and an audio message with waveform, duration, and play button. A centered system line states a disappearing-message timer. The bottom composer combines an add control, message field, sticker, camera, and microphone icons.

screens.name: Signal group video call
screens.layout: The group name and participant count sit above a two-column grid of six large video tiles. A horizontal strip of smaller participant thumbnails follows beneath the grid. A bottom control shelf contains camera, microphone, overflow, and end-call buttons, while individual tiles display small participant status indicators.

screens.name: Signal story viewer
screens.layout: A full-screen portrait photograph forms the story surface, with a close control in the upper-left corner. The author's avatar, name, and relative time sit near the bottom beside an overflow control. A thin progress indicator and centered Reply action overlay the lower edge of the media.

screens.name: Signal attachment picker
screens.layout: The upper conversation area shows text, an audio waveform message, and a document attachment with filename and size. Beneath the composer, a horizontal row of recent photo and video thumbnails leads into labeled attachment choices. Photos, GIF, File, Contact, and a partially visible location option use circular icon buttons.

screens.name: Signal group conversation
screens.layout: A group avatar and title sit in the top bar between back and video controls. The thread contains an image, outgoing text, and incoming messages labeled with individual participant names and accompanied by avatars. Reaction badges appear beneath selected messages, and a message composer with attachment and media controls anchors the bottom.

screens.name: Signal username QR card
screens.layout: A sheet header pairs Done with a Code and Scan segmented control. A large QR card dominates the center and includes the username beneath the code. Three compact actions labeled Link, Share, and Color sit below, followed by explanatory text and a separate Reset control near the bottom.

screens.name: Telegram chat inbox
screens.layout: The Chats header has edit and compose controls above a horizontal strip of circular stories. Filter tabs sit between the stories and the conversation list. Each row combines an avatar, name, latest-message preview, timestamp, and optional unread badge. Bottom navigation includes Contacts, Calls, Chats, Settings, and a separate search button.

screens.name: Telegram group voice recording
screens.layout: The group conversation contains a sticker, a quoted reply, an anonymous poll with horizontal result bars, and an audio message. Sender names appear above relevant bubbles. At the bottom, an active recording strip shows elapsed time and a slide-to-cancel label beside a large microphone control and a lock indicator.

screens.name: Telegram emoji keyboard
screens.layout: A conversation header sits above a multi-image cat collage, a text bubble, and an incoming-call card. The message composer separates the conversation from a large emoji panel. The panel presents category icons and a dense emoji grid, with GIFs, Stickers, and Emoji mode choices along its lower edge.
