screens.name: Telegram secret conversation
screens.layout: A lock icon precedes the contact name in the conversation header. The thread combines alternating text bubbles, a timed media thumbnail, a sticker, and centered system notices about the timer and a screenshot. A bottom message field is flanked by attachment and microphone controls and includes a visible timer indicator.

screens.name: Telegram shared location conversation
screens.layout: The conversation header sits above a live-location card containing a small map. Text bubbles alternate around a dice message and a circular video message with duration. A photograph fills the chat background. The bottom composer includes an attachment control, message field, timer icon, and microphone button.

screens.name: Telegram contact media profile
screens.layout: A centered avatar, contact name, and presence label sit beneath back and Edit controls. A row of call, video, mute, search, and more actions follows. A short bio precedes media-category tabs, and a three-column thumbnail grid fills the lower portion with a mixture of photos and videos.

screens.name: Discord channel emoji picker
screens.layout: The channel header shows a hash-prefixed name and online count above a message thread with avatars and emoji posts. A composer row separates the thread from an expanded picker. Emoji, GIFs, and Stickers tabs sit above a search field, followed by server-specific emoji rows and a compact category strip.

screens.name: Discord video room
screens.layout: A room name and downward chevron sit above a two-column participant grid mixing live video and illustrated avatars. Participant names appear inside the tiles, with microphone or screen indicators on selected tiles. A bottom toolbar groups camera, microphone, sharing, additional-call controls, and a prominent end-call button.

screens.name: Discord direct messages
screens.layout: A narrow vertical server rail occupies the left edge, while the main column begins with Messages, search, Add Friends, and a plus control. Conversation rows pair avatars with names, message previews, and elapsed times. An account strip at the bottom shows the user's avatar, name, presence, and notification control.

screens.name: Discord server channels
screens.layout: A server icon rail borders the channel drawer. The main area starts with a server banner, server name, membership information, and a search field. Chat and Voice Hangout headings separate text-channel rows from a voice channel, with participant avatars and microphone or camera status icons nested beneath the voice channel.

screens.name: Arc Search query suggestions
screens.layout: A rounded search panel occupies the lower part of an otherwise open browser surface. Its input field is followed by vertically stacked recent or suggested query rows. Each row begins with a search icon and ends with a Browse for Me control, giving the query text the largest share of the row.

screens.name: Arc Search generated answer
screens.layout: A query field sits at the top of the answer page. A compact image collage precedes a large answer heading, followed by a single-column sequence of explanatory points. Each point has a small leading icon and a bold topic label, with supporting prose and occasional underlined source references.

screens.name: Arc Search page summary
screens.layout: A compact page title appears above a reduced preview of the original webpage. The summary begins below that preview with an introductory paragraph and continues through titled sections. Circular icons sit beside section headings, while the supporting paragraphs align in a narrower column beneath their respective headings.

screens.name: Arc Search incognito input
screens.layout: A rounded input panel contains an empty search field near its top and a centered incognito-status message beneath it. The on-screen keyboard fills the lower part of the display. The surrounding browser surface is otherwise empty, keeping the active text field and privacy status visually isolated.

screens.name: Arc Search tab previews
screens.layout: Overlapping webpage cards form a horizontal tab stack, with one large central preview and neighboring cards partially visible at either side. Small favicons and page titles sit above the corresponding previews. The central card shows a publication header, section title, image, and article excerpt within the page snapshot.

screens.name: Arc Search voice query
screens.layout: A webpage remains visible behind a translucent voice-search surface. A large listening-face symbol sits in the lower half above the recognized spoken query, which is centered near the bottom. The underlying article's title, byline, and lead photograph remain faintly legible through the overlay.

screens.name: Arc desktop sync introduction
screens.layout: A centered Arc mark leads into a large Sync with Arc Desktop heading and a short explanatory paragraph. The content occupies the middle of a rounded sheet with substantial open space below. A wide Sign in with Arc button appears near the bottom above a partially visible account-creation alternative.

screens.name: Arc default browser instructions
screens.layout: A rounded panel contains a prominent setup heading and short explanation. Three numbered rows list the settings steps, each with a leading icon and concise instruction. A full-width Open Arc Search in Settings button sits below the steps, separated from the text by a small gap.

screens.name: Perplexity answer thread
screens.layout: A Thread toolbar places close and share controls at opposite sides. The query title precedes compact Pro Search and Sources rows with expansion controls. An Answer heading and audio icon introduce an image strip and a subject information card, whose labeled facts continue below the visible screen.

screens.name: Perplexity Discover story
screens.layout: The Discover title sits above a large rounded story card with an audio control near the top toolbar. A prominent photograph occupies the upper part of the card, followed by the article headline and short excerpt. A compact footer presents engagement counts and the story's relative age.

screens.name: Perplexity search clarification
screens.layout: A Thread header and travel query title appear above an expanded Pro Search panel. The panel shows a status line, a question, and selectable interest chips. A labeled free-text field follows the suggested choices, with Skip and Continue buttons aligned side by side at the bottom of the panel.

screens.name: Perplexity research library
screens.layout: The Library header places search and add controls at opposite sides. Library, Pages, and Collections tabs sit above a vertical list of saved questions. Each entry contains a title, short answer excerpt, miniature image strip, and timestamp, with thin dividers separating the research items.

screens.name: Perplexity related questions
screens.layout: The lower portion of an answer fills a continuous text column beneath the Thread toolbar. Inline numbered citations appear near the final paragraph, followed by a row of response actions and an overflow control. A Related heading introduces stacked follow-up questions, each ending with a plus button.

screens.name: Perplexity expanded sources
screens.layout: A question heading sits below the Thread toolbar and above a Pro Search summary row. The Sources section is expanded into horizontally arranged citation cards with titles and source identities. An Answer heading with an audio icon follows beneath, introducing a large image strip at the bottom of the visible area.

screens.name: Perplexity voice answer
screens.layout: A source-count pill sits above a horizontal image carousel whose main card shows a product photograph. Large answer text appears below the images, with the visible spoken portion emphasized against adjacent text. A broad waveform fills the lower area, and the edge of a bottom control is visible beneath it.

screens.name: ChatGPT image conversation
screens.layout: The top bar places a menu control opposite new-chat and overflow actions. Right-aligned prompt bubbles alternate with large image responses in the conversation column. A floating composer overlays the bottom, combining an add button, Ask ChatGPT field, microphone, and circular voice control beneath the latest image.

screens.name: ChatGPT voice conversation
screens.layout: Text prompts appear in right-aligned bubbles above assistant paragraphs with response-action icons. A small voice orb occupies open space near the lower center. The bottom row contains an add button and text field alongside microphone-mute and close controls, while the top bar retains menu and voice-settings controls.

screens.name: ChatGPT text answer
screens.layout: A menu button sits opposite new-chat and overflow controls above the conversation. A right-aligned question bubble precedes several assistant paragraphs, followed by a compact row of copy, audio, feedback, regenerate, and share icons. A rounded composer with attachment, microphone, and voice controls anchors the bottom.

screens.name: ChatGPT image question
screens.layout: A right-aligned uploaded photograph appears above the user's question bubble. The assistant response below uses a heading, subsection labels, and itemized lines with prices. Menu, new-chat, and overflow controls frame the top, while the floating composer overlaps the continuing response at the bottom of the screen.

screens.name: ChatGPT email draft card
screens.layout: A right-aligned request bubble sits above a large embedded Email card. The card contains a recipient area, subject, and formatted message body, with edit, copy, and send icons along its top edge. The surrounding chat retains the top navigation controls and the rounded composer beneath the draft.

screens.name: GitHub mobile home
screens.layout: Home appears beneath add and search buttons. A My Work group lists Issues, Pull Requests, Discussions, Top Repositories, and Organizations as icon-led rows with chevrons. A Favorites group contains repository owners and names. Bottom navigation covers Home, Inbox, Explore, and Profile beside a separate assistant control.

screens.name: GitHub notifications inbox
screens.layout: A Spanish-language inbox heading follows a selection control and precedes horizontal filter chips. A dismissible configuration card occupies the upper content area. Below, notification rows display issue or pull-request icons, repository references, titles, activity snippets, timestamps, unread indicators, and counts. The bottom navigation highlights the inbox destination.

screens.name: GitHub pull request detail
screens.layout: A compact navigation bar sits above the repository reference and pull-request title. A merged badge and branch labels precede author information and a formatted description with links and bullets. A Changes section lists file and commit counts, while comment and information controls float above the bottom navigation.

screens.name: GitHub file diff review
screens.layout: The Files Changed header displays addition and deletion totals beside settings and share controls. Collapsible file headings divide stacked code diffs with line numbers, changed-line markers, and hunk headers. A Show next lines row interrupts one file, and a floating Finish Review control sits above the persistent bottom navigation.

screens.name: Trello planner agenda
screens.layout: A narrow date column accompanies vertically stacked appointment cards grouped by day. Event cards show titles and time ranges, while a focus-time block contains an embedded task. A suggested focus-time slot has a dashed outline and plus button. The bottom navigation highlights Planner among five destinations.

screens.name: Asana project task list
screens.layout: The mobile project header includes back navigation, project name, participant avatars, an add control, and overflow menu. Task name and Assignee column labels sit above collapsible project sections. Individual rows use completion circles at the left and assignee portraits at the right, with a completed item visibly muted.

screens.name: Asana home overview
screens.layout: A Home heading sits above stacked sections. The visible Projects card lists three projects with distinctive leading icons, while its header includes a Starred filter and chevron. A My Tasks card begins below with a Due soon selector. Rounded section containers and overflow controls organize the overview vertically.

screens.name: Asana inbox activity
screens.layout: An Inbox heading and overflow control lead into a relevance label and stacked update cards. Each update identifies its project and task before showing an author avatar and message or activity summary. Due-date and unread indicators appear beside selected entries, and reaction controls align along the right edge.

screens.name: Asana My Tasks
screens.layout: The My Tasks heading has an overflow control above collapsible task groups with counts. Visible rows pair completion circles with task names, project subtitles, priority labels, and right-aligned due dates. A floating New task button anchors the lower-right corner while additional task rows continue beneath the current group.

screens.name: Asana task detail
screens.layout: A top action row contains back, Mark complete, reaction, link, and overflow controls. The task title is followed by assignee and due-date controls. Projects and custom-field sections precede a Google Drive attachment card with ownership and comment metadata, then a Description section containing the task's body text.

screens.name: Asana search results
screens.layout: An entered query and clear control occupy the search field above category tabs. Results are divided into Tasks and Projects sections. Task rows pair completion icons, titles, project subtitles, and assignee avatars; project rows use larger project icons and team subtitles. Show more links follow each visible section.

screens.name: Miro mood board canvas
screens.layout: A compact header contains back navigation, board title, search, collaborator avatars, and overflow. The dotted canvas holds a collage of images, sticky notes, swatches, and labels, with named collaborator cursors among the objects. Undo and redo controls float at the left, while separate tool and add buttons occupy the bottom corners.

screens.name: Miro prioritization matrix
screens.layout: A board toolbar with back, title, search, collaborators, and overflow sits above a dotted canvas. A four-quadrant matrix labeled with impact and effort organizes nearby sticky notes. Named collaborator cursors and a comment badge appear around the diagram, while undo, redo, tools, and add controls float at the canvas edges.

screens.name: Miro board comment thread
screens.layout: The upper canvas shows sticky notes connected by arrows, named collaborator cursors, and a comment marker. A bottom sheet covers the lower canvas with a Resolve switch, thread indicators, and stacked comments containing avatars, names, timestamps, and reactions. A reply field and mention control run along the sheet's bottom edge.

screens.name: Miro document text editing
screens.layout: The board header sits above a document object whose title text is selected. A secondary heading and paragraph follow within the document. A formatting toolbar above the keyboard includes heading style, bold, alignment, annotation, link, and comment controls. A Done control appears between the formatting row and on-screen keyboard.

screens.name: Miro add tools sheet
screens.layout: A board toolbar and floating undo controls remain visible above a canvas containing a large sticky note and connector. A rounded bottom sheet presents a labeled grid of creation tools: Text, Sticky note, Stickies capture, Comment, Pen, Shapes, Document, Frame, and Upload, each represented by an icon.

screens.name: Miro lock-screen notifications
screens.layout: The system lock screen displays the date and large time above three stacked Miro notification cards. Each card includes the app icon, board title, author-prefixed message preview, and timestamp aligned to the right. Flashlight and camera shortcuts sit at opposite bottom corners beneath the notification group.

screens.name: Audio Player — waveform playback
screens.layout: A centered title and artist sit above a waveform spanning almost the entire window. A vertical playhead crosses the waveform, with elapsed and total times below. The bottom row places speed at left, skip and pause controls centrally, and volume at right.

screens.name: Calculator — basic history
screens.layout: The narrow window stacks a mode selector, a large expression history, and a keypad. Previous equations align expressions on the left and results on the right. The current value occupies its own row above five columns of numeric and arithmetic controls, including a tall equals button.

screens.name: Calculator — advanced keypad
screens.layout: A mode selector anchors the header above an expression history with right-aligned answers. The lower half expands into a dense scientific keypad. Function columns sit left of the numeric block, while arithmetic operators and a tall equals button occupy the right edge.

screens.name: Calendar — month grid
screens.layout: A seven-column month grid fills the window beneath a centered month label. Each date cell contains compact event strips, with some events spanning adjacent dates. Bottom navigation places date controls at left, Month and Week switches centrally, and a plus action at right.

screens.name: Calendar — week schedule
screens.layout: Seven dated columns sit beneath the month header, with all-day events collected across their tops. An hourly grid occupies the remaining area and contains event blocks of differing heights. Navigation and Today controls sit at bottom left, with Month and Week switches centered below.

screens.name: Camera — capture preview
screens.layout: The narrow camera window centers a landscape preview between open vertical margins. A header groups timer, photo and video modes, menu, and close controls. A large circular shutter sits below the preview, with a small image thumbnail offset to its left.

screens.name: Camera — captured image review
screens.layout: A captured landscape image is centered within a tall review window with substantial space above and below. A back arrow sits at the upper left and a menu at the upper right. Small previous and next controls appear below the image, opposite an external-opening icon.

screens.name: Characters — emoji browser
screens.layout: A fixed left sidebar groups recently used items, emoji categories, and letter or symbol categories beneath search and menu controls. Food and Drink is selected. The wider main pane uses a regular icon grid under its category title, with large individual food symbols and no explanatory cards.

screens.name: Characters — letter browser
screens.layout: The left sidebar is scrolled to letter and symbol categories, with Letters selected near the bottom. The main pane presents oversized individual glyphs in a ruled grid under a centered title. Search and menu controls remain above the sidebar, separate from the glyph browsing area.

screens.name: Clocks — world times
screens.layout: A top tab strip offers World, Alarms, Stopwatch, and Timer, with a plus button at the left edge. A compact central card lists four cities. Each row pairs a location and offset description with a prominent time badge and a small remove control.

screens.name: Clocks — alarm list
screens.layout: The Alarms tab is selected in a four-part header navigation, beside a separate plus action. A central card contains three alarm rows. Large times sit left, with repeat-day or label details below; individual enable switches and removal controls align on the right of each row.

screens.name: Connections — add remote connection
screens.layout: A small connection popover opens from the header plus button over a mostly empty workspace. It contains a network identifier field, two connection-type radio choices, and Help and Connect buttons. Behind it, a centered application symbol and welcome text explain the unpopulated connection area.

screens.name: Connections — remote desktop session
screens.layout: An outer application header identifies the remote computer and places session controls along its right edge. The remote desktop fills the content area, showing an overview search field, a workspace preview containing two app windows, a partial adjacent workspace, and a centered application dock below.

screens.name: Console — terminal output
screens.layout: A compact header places search on the left, the working-directory marker centrally, and new-tab and menu controls on the right. Monospaced terminal output begins at the upper left, followed by a shell prompt and block cursor. Most of the remaining command area is empty.

screens.name: Contacts — no selected contact
screens.layout: The window is divided into a narrow contacts sidebar and a larger detail pane. The sidebar contains a header with add, selection, and menu controls above a search field. The otherwise empty detail pane centers a person symbol and the instruction to select a contact.

screens.name: Contacts — selected person
screens.layout: A searchable sidebar groups favorites above all contacts, with portraits and names in vertically stacked rows. The selected person opens in a larger pane with a portrait and bold name. Email, phone, and birthday appear as separate cards, while favorite, edit, and delete controls occupy the header.

screens.name: Disk Usage Analyzer — device selection
screens.layout: A centered content column under the Devices and Locations title begins with a This Computer heading. A rounded list contains a Home Folder row and a disk row, each ending in a chevron. The disk row adds available and total capacity labels above a horizontal usage bar.

screens.name: Disk Usage Analyzer — folder breakdown
screens.layout: A toolbar with back navigation and a Home Folder path sits above two adjacent analysis panes. The left pane is an expandable folder table with size, contents, and modified columns. The right pane contains a large concentric segmented chart, with chart-style controls centered beneath it.

screens.name: Disks — selected disk overview
screens.layout: A narrow sidebar lists three disks with the selected device highlighted. The main pane begins with a disk icon, capacity title, model subtitle, and utility controls. A space-allocation bar precedes a volumes list, where each row includes a name, mount detail, usage bar, menu, and disclosure control.

screens.name: Disks — format volume dialog
screens.layout: A centered Format Volume dialog overlays the selected disk screen. Cancel and Next flank its title. The form stacks a volume-name field, an overwrite switch, a filesystem radio group with supporting text, and a password-protection switch, while the disk sidebar remains visible behind the dialog.

screens.name: Document Scanner — scanned page preview
screens.layout: A portrait page preview sits centrally with a boundary and ruler marks around its edges. The header shows Stop, settings, export, and menu controls. A bottom toolbar places New Document at left and groups rotation, crop, and delete icons directly below the preview.

screens.name: Document Viewer — document with outline
screens.layout: A left outline pane lists section titles with page numbers and a row of pane-mode icons at its foot. The larger document pane shows a cover page and the beginning of the following page. Its header includes the filename and page counter, with floating zoom controls near the lower right.

screens.name: Document Viewer — narrow outline overlay
screens.layout: In the narrow window, the document outline occupies most of the width and leaves only a slim portion of the page visible to its right. Section names and page numbers form a vertical list. Search and menu sit above, with outline-mode controls along the bottom edge.

screens.name: Files — home folder grid
screens.layout: A navigation sidebar separates general locations from personal folders. The main pane places large labeled folder icons in a spacious grid below a breadcrumb toolbar. Back and forward controls sit before Home, while search, view selection, and menu controls align at the opposite end of the header.

screens.name: Files — home folder table
screens.layout: The sidebar retains location and personal-folder navigation beside a wide file table. Name, Size, and Modified headings sit above eight folder rows. Each row begins with a folder icon and ends with a star control, while navigation, location, search, and view controls remain in the toolbar.

screens.name: Fonts — font collection
screens.layout: A centered search field occupies the top toolbar, accompanied by an information control at the right. Below it, font samples form a three-column grid. Each tile uses a large Aa specimen above a small font-name label, with additional rows continuing beyond the visible lower edge.

screens.name: Fonts — specimen detail
screens.layout: A back control leads the header, while the selected family and style are centered and Info and Installed controls sit right. The content begins with a large font name, followed by alphabet and numeral samples. Repeated specimen sentences increase in size down the page.

screens.name: Help — topic overview
screens.layout: A browser-like header contains back and forward navigation plus bookmark, search, and menu controls. Under the GNOME Help heading, full-width topic rows pair bold titles with explanatory lines. Introductory topics appear first, followed by category rows with large icons at the left.

screens.name: Image Viewer — photo view
screens.layout: A single photograph fills nearly all of the window below a compact header. The filename is centered above the image. Fullscreen sits at the left, while crop, information, and menu controls are grouped at the right, keeping the image itself free of persistent side panels.

screens.name: Image Viewer — crop editor
screens.layout: The editor divides its body into an image preview on the left and controls on the right. A rectangular crop boundary overlays the photo. The control column groups aspect-ratio presets, orientation choices, rotation buttons, and flip buttons, while Cancel and Save occupy opposite header corners.

screens.name: Logs — application messages
screens.layout: A slim left navigation rail lists severity and source categories, with Applications selected. The larger pane contains closely stacked monospaced log rows, some with small count badges and timestamps aligned at the right. A date-range title, search, export, and menu controls share the header.

screens.name: Maps — regional map
screens.layout: A map occupies the full content area beneath a thin toolbar with a centered search field. Place labels and roads are embedded directly in the map. Small circular map controls cluster at the lower right, and a compact scale and attribution sit along the lower edge.

screens.name: Maps — route directions
screens.layout: A narrow directions pane sits to the left of a large map. Its top contains travel-mode controls and start and destination fields, followed by an estimated duration and turn-by-turn list. The map displays the route between marked endpoints, with view controls at the lower right.

screens.name: Music — album collection
screens.layout: A top navigation strip offers Albums, Artists, Songs, and Playlists, followed by search and utility controls. The content uses a four-column album grid with square covers. Each cover has its title and artist underneath, and further albums continue below the visible area.

screens.name: Music — album tracks and playback
screens.layout: The album detail begins with cover art beside the album title, artist, duration, and play controls. A numbered track list below aligns titles left and durations and menus right. A persistent bottom player shows the current track, transport controls, a progress slider, and a queue control.

screens.name: Settings — appearance
screens.layout: A category sidebar anchors the left edge with Appearance selected. The main pane groups two large style previews above a Background section. An Add Picture action aligns with that heading, while selectable background thumbnails form a multi-column grid extending below the viewport.

screens.name: Settings — sound
screens.layout: A category sidebar highlights Sound beside a stacked settings pane. Output groups a device selector, Test button, volume slider, and balance slider. Input has its own device selector and volume control. A separate Sounds section below contains a Volume Levels row with a trailing chevron.

screens.name: Software — explore catalog
screens.layout: Explore, Installed, and Updates tabs span the header between search and menu controls. A wide featured-app carousel leads the content with an app icon, title, and short description. Two rows of category buttons follow, and an Editor’s Choice section begins at the lower edge.

screens.name: Software — app detail
screens.layout: The app detail header pairs an icon and product name with publisher and rating information. An Install button and source selector align to the right. Below, a screenshot carousel occupies most of the width, with pagination dots and an arrow before the descriptive section begins.

screens.name: System Monitor — filtered processes
screens.layout: Processes, Resources, and File Systems tabs sit above an active search field. A dense process table fills the window with columns for name, CPU, identifier, memory, disk activity, and priority. One row is selected, and an End Process button sits at the bottom left.

screens.name: System Monitor — CPU resources
screens.layout: The Resources tab is selected above an expanded CPU section. A large time-series plot spans the pane, followed by a multi-column legend of processor labels and percentages. Memory and Swap, Network, and Disk remain collapsed as labeled disclosure rows beneath the chart.

screens.name: Text Editor — tabbed Markdown file
screens.layout: The header contains Open and new-document actions, a centered filename and directory, and utility controls at the right. A second strip holds three document tabs. The selected Markdown document fills the editing area with syntax-colored source text and no visible sidebar or preview pane.

screens.name: Tour — introduction slide
screens.layout: A small progress-dot row sits near the top of the window above a large centered illustration. A bold Start the Tour heading and short explanatory sentence follow beneath it. A circular next arrow appears midway along the right edge, with the close control in the upper corner.

screens.name: Video Player — video playback
screens.layout: The video fills the player, with overlay controls placed over the image. Pause and skip controls sit in the center. Near the bottom, a title appears above a long seek bar, elapsed and total times sit below, and volume and utility controls occupy the lower right.

screens.name: Weather — hourly forecast
screens.layout: The top bar offers Hourly and Daily modes. A location dropdown, condition icon, and large current temperature lead the content. Below, hourly columns align times, weather symbols, and temperatures across a continuous filled trend chart, with a next control at right and update text underneath.

screens.name: Weather — daily forecast
screens.layout: Hourly and Daily mode switches sit above a current-condition summary with location and temperature. The lower pane divides upcoming days into equal vertical columns, each containing a date, condition icon, high and low temperatures, and overflow control. A right-edge arrow advances the visible forecast range.

screens.name: Web — browser page
screens.layout: A browser toolbar places back, forward, reload, and new-tab controls before an address field, with page and menu controls at the right. The webpage below has its own site header, a large application banner, and a readable article section headed Browse the web.

screens.name: Amberol — playlist beside player
screens.layout: A narrow playlist pane lists track artwork, titles, and artists beneath a remaining-time summary. The adjacent player centers cover art above a waveform, times, and track metadata. Transport controls, a volume slider, and a final row of utility buttons sit below the selected track.

screens.name: Amberol — compact player
screens.layout: The compact window removes the visible playlist and stacks all player content vertically. Cover art leads a waveform and elapsed and remaining times. Track title, artist, and album sit above transport controls, followed by a volume slider and a small row of utility icons.

screens.name: Apostrophe — Markdown writing
screens.layout: Open and Save controls sit at the left of a header centered on the document filename. The main writing area displays Markdown source in a restrained central column. A bottom toolbar collects formatting icons, while the character count is aligned at the opposite corner.

screens.name: Audio Sharing — stream address
screens.layout: A compact window centers a large QR code above a stream address and Copy to Clipboard button. A dividing line separates those primary elements from explanatory text about accessing the shared audio. The title sits between a menu control and close button in the header.

screens.name: Authenticator — account codes
screens.layout: The window header places add, search, and menu actions around the title. Provider headings with icons separate a vertical series of account cards. Each card aligns the account label left and its code right, followed by copy and detail controls; small progress indicators appear beside some providers.

screens.name: Authenticator — add account
screens.layout: A back arrow and Add button flank the Add a New Account title. A large provider icon leads a grouped form with Provider, Account, and masked Token fields. Additional rows show algorithm, computing method, period, digits, website, and setup guidance, with secondary descriptions below several labels.

screens.name: Bazaar — app discovery
screens.layout: Explore, Library, and Search navigation sits above a large featured-app banner containing product artwork and a screenshot. A segmented filter row follows the banner. Below it, compact app cards form a four-column grid, each pairing an icon with name, description, and occasional installed status.

screens.name: Bazaar — app detail
screens.layout: An app icon and title appear beside publisher badges, opposite a prominent Install button. A horizontal row summarizes download size, software status, safety, device availability, age suitability, and popularity. A screenshot carousel follows, then a bold descriptive heading and a paragraph about the app.

screens.name: Biblioteca — API documentation
screens.layout: A searchable tree of libraries and API namespaces fills the left pane. The selected namespace expands to reveal grouped reference sections. The wider reading pane begins with a namespace heading and metadata, followed by Build and Dependencies sections with aligned labels, values, and linked reference text.

screens.name: Binary — number-base conversion
screens.layout: A small window stacks two conversion sections with generous separation. The upper section pairs a Binary dropdown and bit-width selector above an editable value field. A swap icon divides it from the Decimal selector and output field below, with menu and close controls in the header.

screens.name: Blanket — ambient sound mixer
screens.layout: A preset dropdown and menu flank the title above a four-column sound grid. Each sound has a large pictogram, name, and individual volume slider. Additional sounds continue below the visible rows, while a bottom bar centers playback between a mute control and overflow menu.

screens.name: Boatswain — device button editor
screens.layout: The window uses three regions: a device and profile sidebar, a central six-button arrangement, and a Button Properties pane. One button is selected in the central grid. Its properties show an icon preview, editable name, background control, device and profile choices, and a Remove Action button.

screens.name: Boatswain — action browser
screens.layout: A narrow action browser has a back arrow and Actions title at the top. Expandable groups divide a vertical list into Soundboard, OBS Studio, and Network sections. Individual actions have small leading icons, with occasional secondary descriptions underneath, and the lower entries extend past the viewport.

screens.name: Bobby — database table search
screens.layout: A table selector occupies the upper left while an active search field sits near the center of the header. The table below has numbered rows and four named columns. Matching text is emphasized within cells, and one complete row is selected across the table width.

screens.name: Bobby — table preferences
screens.layout: A Preferences dialog overlays the database table, leaving its selected row visible behind. Rows and Columns groups a row-number switch, row-order selector, and column-separator selector. A separate Appearance group contains a monospace-font switch, with a close control in the dialog’s upper-right corner.

screens.name: Bustle — message sequence timeline
screens.layout: A Record control, open action, and filter icon occupy the toolbar above a logged-message count. The main area aligns message timestamps, source names, and method identifiers at left with a sequence chart at right. Vertical participant lines and horizontal arrows show individual message relationships.

screens.name: Bustle — duration statistics
screens.layout: Frequencies, Durations, and Sizes switches form the top navigation, with Durations selected. The body is a dense statistics table listing method names alongside total duration, call count, and mean duration. Small inline bars accompany the call column, and the table extends below the visible window.

screens.name: Chess Clock — active match
screens.layout: The window is split into two equally prominent timer regions, each centered around a large countdown value. A circular menu control straddles the dividing line at the top. A circular pause control occupies the same central line near the bottom, with close at the upper right.

screens.name: Chess Clock — time setup
screens.layout: A welcome heading and short instruction introduce a centered configuration card. Two rows of preset time buttons sit above separate minute, second, and increment counters with plus and minus controls. A final row pairs the Time control method label with an Increment dropdown.

screens.name: Citations — reference detail
screens.layout: A narrow reference list shows author names, years, and abbreviated titles beneath add and search controls. The selected item opens as a Book detail in the right pane. Citation type, key, author, title, year, and DOI occupy stacked editable rows, with further properties below.

screens.name: Clairvoyant — answer result
screens.layout: The small window centers a single large answer sentence above an Ask Again button. These two elements occupy the middle of an otherwise open content area. An information control sits in the upper-left corner, balanced by the close control at the upper right.

screens.name: Collision — generated hashes
screens.layout: Open, Hash, and Verify controls span the header, with Hash selected. A bold filename and directory appear above a stacked card of checksum rows. Each row labels its algorithm, displays a monospaced hash across one or more lines, and places a copy button at the right.

screens.name: Collision — verification comparison
screens.layout: The Verify mode is selected above a centered filename and directory. Two labeled columns, Checksum and File, sit side by side beneath them. One contains a multiline checksum with a check indicator; the other contains a large failure mark and a shortened comparison filename.

screens.name: Commit — commit message editor
screens.layout: Abort and Commit buttons flank a branch-specific header. A monospaced text editor fills the body with a short subject, blank-line separation, and a longer description. Part of the subject is highlighted, and commented guidance continues below; a circular menu control floats at the lower right.

screens.name: Commit — keyboard shortcuts
screens.layout: A search control and Shortcuts title sit above two shortcut groups. Editing occupies the larger left area, while General forms a smaller right column. Each entry pairs keycap-shaped combinations with a plain-language action label, leaving generous spacing between the groups and the window edges.

screens.name: Concessio — permission calculator
screens.layout: Permissions and Umask tabs sit above an Open File row. Numeric and Symbolic values appear in paired fields with copy and validity indicators. A grouped panel below lists User, Group, and Others, each with read, write, execute, and additional permission controls aligned in columns.

screens.name: Concessio — loaded file permissions
screens.layout: The Permissions tab is selected above a loaded-file row containing a filename, directory, folder control, remove control, and apply checkmark. Paired Numeric and Symbolic fields follow. Below, User, Group, and Others rows expose aligned permission icons and supplemental mode dropdowns within one grouped panel.

screens.name: Constrict — queued video export
screens.layout: A left settings column groups target size, framerate radio choices, encoding options, and advanced tolerance controls. The larger pane lists four video sources with thumbnails, filenames, dimensions, and row menus. Add Videos sits beneath the list, and Export To is centered near the bottom.

screens.name: Constrict — export in progress
screens.layout: The header reports that two of four videos have been processed, with an export location beneath. The source list shows completed checkmarks and a progress indicator beside individual files. Settings in the left column appear subdued, and a Cancel control replaces the export action at the bottom.

screens.name: Curtail — compressed image results
screens.layout: A title and mode subtitle sit above a compact results card near the top of the window. Three image rows pair thumbnails and filenames with original and resulting sizes. Savings percentages align at the far right, while open and refresh controls sit at the header’s left.

screens.name: Curtail — general preferences
screens.layout: General and Compression tabs occupy the top of a compact preferences window. A grouped panel contains a Safe Mode switch and editable filename suffix, followed by switches for metadata and file attributes. The final row presents a compression timeout with a numeric value and stepper buttons.

screens.name: Déjà Dup Backups — backup overview
screens.layout: A grouped central card summarizes schedule, most recent backup, included folders, and storage location. Navigable rows end in chevrons, while a Browse Backups action spans the card’s bottom. A prominent Back Up Now button sits below the card, with the app menu in the header.

screens.name: Déjà Dup Backups — backup history
screens.layout: A back arrow precedes the Backups title in the header. The main content is a compact card containing four backup timestamps as separate rows. Each row ends with an external-opening control. The remainder of the window is open space, keeping the dated recovery points prominent.

screens.name: Decoder — QR creation
screens.layout: Create, Scan, and History tabs sit above a large QR preview. A Text and Wi-Fi segmented control appears beneath the preview, followed by a multiline content field. Export and Save buttons share the bottom row, while menu and close controls remain in the header.

screens.name: Decoder — QR scanning
screens.layout: The Scan tab is selected in a top navigation strip alongside Create and History. A camera image containing a large QR code dominates the central area. Below the image, two small scan-related controls occupy the lower center, with the surrounding preview region otherwise free of panels.

screens.name: Dialect — translation panes
screens.layout: Two text panes fill the window beneath source and target language selectors, separated by a swap control. The source pane has text tools, a character count, and a Translate button along its bottom. The translated pane places copy and speaker controls at its lower-right corner.

screens.name: Dialect — language selector
screens.layout: A language-selection popover opens below the target-language selector over the right translation pane. It starts with a search field, followed by a selected-language row with a checkmark and a vertical language list. Source text and the Translate action remain visible in the adjacent pane.

screens.name: Drum Machine — step sequencer
screens.layout: Named percussion tracks form rows along the left of a large step grid, with groups of square cells aligned across each row. Open and utility controls occupy the header. A tempo stepper sits at the lower left, playback and sound controls centrally, and Reset at the lower right.

screens.name: Ear Tag — audio metadata editor
screens.layout: A left file list shows track artwork and abbreviated names beneath save and search controls. The selected track opens in a larger pane with cover art, navigation arrows, title, artist, and technical metadata. Editable track number, album, album artist, genre, and date fields stack below.

screens.name: Ear Tag — compact metadata editor
screens.layout: The narrow window presents the selected track without the persistent file list. Cover art and previous and next arrows lead title, artist, and technical details. Two small track-count fields sit side by side above stacked album, album artist, and genre rows, each with an edit control.

screens.name: Elastic — spring preview controls
screens.layout: A Basic and Interactive switch sits above a preview containing several simple shapes. Initial velocity appears below with a slider, numeric stepper, and play control. Damping, mass, stiffness, and epsilon occupy a two-column parameter grid, followed by a code panel with language tabs.

screens.name: Elastic — spring response graph
screens.layout: A response curve fills the upper preview beneath Basic and Interactive switches, with duration and minimum and maximum values along its base. An initial-velocity slider and play control sit below. A two-column parameter panel follows, and code-language tabs begin at the bottom of the window.

screens.name: Emblem — icon composition
screens.layout: The compact editor divides controls from a dedicated preview pane. Stacked segmented controls choose fill mode, appearance, and shape, above a Choose Symbolic button. A tall swatch control sits beside them. The preview pane shows the composed icon with PNG and SVG export buttons underneath.

screens.name: Errands — expanded task list
screens.layout: A sidebar lists Today, Tags, Trash, and named task lists with counts. The selected Shopping List opens beside an Add new Task field. Task cards contain completion circles, titles, progress summaries, and nested subtasks; one expanded card exposes tags, a date, utility icons, and a subtask entry field.

screens.name: Exercise Timer — active exercise
screens.layout: A back arrow and exercise name sit above a large central timer panel. The panel stacks the Exercise label, countdown, and reset, pause, and sound controls. Beneath it, a thin segmented interval strip spans the width with a small position marker below.

screens.name: Exercise Timer — routines
screens.layout: A plus button and menu flank the Exercise Timer title. The body contains a vertically stacked list of routines. Each row pairs a bold exercise name and interval summary on the left with total duration at the right, followed by separate edit and delete buttons.

screens.name: Eyedropper — color formats
screens.layout: A compact window places an eyedropper action beside the title and a menu at the opposite edge. A wide sample swatch leads a vertical series of value rows. The rows show a name and several color encodings in monospaced text, each ending with a copy button.

screens.name: Eyedropper — color history
screens.layout: A wide selected-color swatch sits above a vertical list of color-format values, each with a right-aligned copy control. A slim column of three recent swatches runs beside the content. The header retains an eyedropper action, title, menu, and close control above the value list.

screens.name: File Shredder — active queue
screens.layout: A small queue card near the top contains two filenames with their full paths beneath. Circular progress indicators align at the far right of each row. A single Abort All button is centered near the bottom of the otherwise open window, below the File Shredder title.

screens.name: Forge Sparks — notification inbox
screens.layout: A Mark all as Read action sits at the left of the header opposite the menu. A grouped list fills the upper body with development notifications. Each row has a leading event icon, title and repository text, with age and author information aligned toward the right.

screens.name: Forge Sparks — background preferences
screens.layout: A compact Preferences window contains one grouped settings panel. Keep Running in Background has an enabled switch and an upward disclosure control. Run on Startup appears as a subordinate row, with Start Hidden beneath it in a subdued state, and a close control at the upper right.

screens.name: Fragments — torrent queue
screens.layout: Add, search, and menu actions surround the Fragments title. The content groups torrents into Downloading, Queued, and Seeding sections. Download rows combine names, transfer details, progress bars, and pause buttons; queued rows add ordering controls, while seeding rows expose remove actions at the right.

screens.name: Fragments — torrent detail
screens.layout: A centered torrent-detail dialog overlays the queue. An icon and filename lead a progress bar with transferred size and remaining time. Pause, Open, Remove, and More form an action row above paired transfer-stat cards, followed by individual file rows with their own progress indicators.

screens.name: Fretboard — chord diagram
screens.layout: A large fretboard diagram occupies the upper center of a compact window, with string markers above and numbered fret navigation at the right. Finger positions are shown as filled circles on the grid. A chord-name band sits below, followed by a favorite icon and View Variants action.

screens.name: Gaphor — model diagram editor
screens.layout: A hierarchical model tree and grouped drawing tools occupy the left sidebar. The central canvas contains connected diagram elements under multiple diagram tabs. A selected element has visible handles, while the right inspector stacks its name, type settings, attributes, operations, and display toggles.

screens.name: Gaphor — sequence diagram editor
screens.layout: A model tree and categorized tool palette sit to the left of a large diagram canvas. Two lifelines and message arrows occupy the center, with one participant selected using corner handles. The right inspector shows Lifeline properties, a name field, connectable-element selector, and note area.

screens.name: Gradia — screenshot background editor
screens.layout: A tall left toolbox groups annotation icons, swatches, a thickness slider, background-mode choices, and gradient controls. The larger preview area displays a screenshot inset within a background. Export and utility actions line the toolbox footer, while crop, zoom, undo, and delete controls sit along the preview’s bottom.

screens.name: Gradia — annotated screenshot
screens.layout: The left toolbox exposes drawing and annotation tools, color swatches, stroke width, and an Image Background selector with a thumbnail. The preview contains a code screenshot with a drawn arrow and obscured lines. Image manipulation and zoom controls remain positioned around the lower edge of the preview.

screens.name: Graphs — plotted functions
screens.layout: A left sidebar lists two enabled functions with color indicators and menus. Below it, grouped controls offer adding, selecting, adjusting, transforming, and modifying data. The main canvas displays both curves on labeled axes with gridlines and a legend, beneath project and view controls in the header.

screens.name: Hieroglyphic — drawn symbol search
screens.layout: The window divides into a large drawing area and a narrower results pane. A hand-drawn symbol occupies the left canvas above a Clear button. The right pane lists candidate mathematical symbols with package labels, command names, and mode details, each ending with a copy control.

screens.name: Triage inbox
screens.layout: A compact team breadcrumb and Triage heading sit above a dense issue list. Each row gives the issue title priority, with a quieter source or author beneath and an identifier aligned to the right. Utility controls remain in the list header.
screens.lesson: Keep intake scannable by repeating a restrained two-line row anatomy.

screens.name: Triage rule settings
screens.layout: A settings heading and creation action lead into separate rule containers. Each rule names its purpose and update metadata before compact condition and resulting-action rows. Repeated When and Then labels make the relationship between criteria and routing visible.
screens.lesson: Express automation rules as readable conditions and outcomes before exposing complex syntax.

screens.name: Customer request overview
screens.layout: Customer identity sits above a compact horizontal properties strip containing relationship metadata. A Requests section follows as a categorized issue list, with request titles leading and priority or recency information aligned toward the edge.
screens.lesson: Keep customer context visible while reviewing the work associated with that customer.

screens.name: Project overview with resource chips
screens.layout: A prominent project name and short description precede compact properties and relationship chips. Resources form a separate line of labeled links, while a latest-update panel introduces a longer progress narrative below the structured metadata.
screens.lesson: Separate factual project properties from narrative progress and reference material.

screens.name: Project team selection
screens.layout: Project properties remain visible behind an anchored team selector. The picker groups teams hierarchically with small symbols and checked selections. Its placement ties the open options to the field being edited rather than opening an unrelated full-page form.
screens.lesson: Preserve object context while editing a multi-value relationship.

screens.name: Initiative portfolio table
screens.layout: A view heading and status tabs frame a table of initiatives. Names occupy the widest leading column, while target period, health, project progress and activity appear in narrow aligned columns. Status symbols and small counts support scanning across rows.
screens.lesson: Use aligned columns when the task requires comparing many related objects.

screens.name: Initiative update preview
screens.layout: A list of initiatives remains in the background while a floating update panel reveals the selected initiative's status, author, time and longer narrative. Small response controls appear beneath the prose, and an update action sits in the panel header.
screens.lesson: Use a readable preview to expose narrative detail without losing the collection context.

screens.name: Initiative overview and latest update
screens.layout: The initiative title and summary lead into compact properties and resources. The latest update occupies a larger editorial region with status, author and timestamp above paragraphs and response actions. Main view tabs remain near the top of the page.
screens.lesson: Allocate different visual space to structured metadata and longer progress reporting.

screens.name: Issue creation dialog
screens.layout: A bounded dialog prioritizes issue title and description. Team and template controls sit above the text, while suggested labels and compact property chips sit below. Attachment, create-another and primary creation controls occupy the final action row.
screens.lesson: Keep writing dominant while allowing useful issue metadata to be set in place.

screens.name: Recurring issue configuration
screens.layout: The issue composer remains the main context while its additional-actions menu exposes scheduling options. The example also shows a recurrence configuration row beneath the editor, using date and repeat controls near the creation action. It is one documented scheduling state, not two counted screens.
screens.lesson: Place recurring scheduling close to the object being created.

screens.name: Cycle detail with progress graph
screens.layout: An issue list remains visible beside a narrow cycle-detail pane. The pane combines a date range, cycle identity and progress counts above a time-series chart, with labels that distinguish scope, started work and completed work.
screens.lesson: Pair trend evidence with the actual work collection it summarizes.

screens.name: Cycle configuration
screens.layout: A settings title and explanation precede an enable toggle. A separate grouped panel aligns configuration labels on the left and selected duration, cooldown, start day and future-cycle values on the right. The primary setting is visually separated from its dependent parameters.
screens.lesson: Distinguish enabling a capability from configuring its schedule.

screens.name: Release issues and properties
screens.layout: A release breadcrumb leads into an issue list grouped by completion state. A right-hand pane presents release identity, release metadata and property tabs, keeping the selected release's summary visible alongside its associated work.
screens.lesson: Use a side pane when list scanning and object context are needed together.

screens.name: Issue release metadata popover
screens.layout: Issue rows expose compact release metadata beside other identifiers. An anchored popover expands one release value into multiple named release entries and dates while surrounding rows remain visible. The interaction is shown as an open state, without timing evidence.
screens.lesson: Reveal additional relationship detail at the point where the compact value appears.

screens.name: Code review workspace
screens.layout: A multi-pane workspace places navigation at the left, a large code-diff area in the center and a narrow discussion or activity pane at the right. File sections and line changes organize the central content; review actions occupy stable upper controls.
screens.lesson: Protect the primary comparison area while retaining navigation and review context.

screens.name: Repository integration settings
screens.layout: Provider identity and a short description sit above compact integration metadata. A connected-organizations section lists an organization with its current capabilities and an adjacent enable-review action; connected-account information appears in a separate lower row.
screens.lesson: Associate configuration actions with the exact connected organization they affect.

screens.name: Code review preferences with preview
screens.layout: A preferences page groups review enablement, pull-request handling and merge strategy above theme and font choices. A code example demonstrates the formatting choices in place, while notification preferences form a lower section. Labels, explanations and trailing controls follow a stable alignment.
screens.lesson: Place a meaningful preview beside appearance choices instead of relying on names alone.

screens.name: Document with assistant task result
screens.layout: A document remains readable in the main area while a compact assistant panel overlays the lower right. The panel contains the instruction, a progress/result summary and a list of created issue references, visually linking the operation to the source document.
screens.lesson: Keep source material and generated work references together during assisted operations.

screens.name: Coding-agent configuration
screens.layout: A settings heading and explanation introduce the enabled agent capability. A separate configuration group aligns agent and model labels with selected values, with short helper text explaining each choice. The page distinguishes the capability state from the options used to run it.
screens.lesson: Separate activation from operational settings so configuration remains understandable.

screens.name: Scheduled automation editor
screens.layout: The automation's name and execution context sit above a Trigger section. Compact schedule controls encode start date and repetition in one group; a distinct Instructions section follows with an optional prompt-suggestion affordance. The screenshot shows configuration rather than execution results.
screens.lesson: Separate when an automation runs from what it should do.

screens.name: New automation starting state
screens.layout: A stable workspace sidebar leads to a spacious creation area. The main prompt field is centered below the page heading, followed by a small grid of suggested use cases. The suggestions are secondary starting points rather than competing primary actions.
screens.lesson: Offer concrete starting examples without obscuring the user's own input path.

screens.name: Assignee and delegation menu
screens.layout: An issue detail remains behind its properties pane. The assignment control opens a menu with people and agent-related choices; a nested delegation submenu extends from the selected item. Small symbols distinguish destination types while the issue context remains visible.
screens.lesson: Use contextual selection to clarify who owns work and who executes a delegated action.

screens.name: Assignment suggestion explanation
screens.layout: An issue's suggestion panel exposes an anchored explanation for a proposed assignee. The explanation lists supporting reasons, shows an alternative and provides an explicit acceptance action below. The underlying issue title and properties remain visible.
screens.lesson: Explain consequential recommendations near the choice and preserve an explicit acceptance step.

screens.name: Assistant conversation pending response
screens.layout: A floating conversation window contains a title bar, dated prompt message and a visible thinking state in the response area. The composer stays at the bottom with compact action controls, while the large empty middle area is reserved for the pending answer.
screens.lesson: Represent pending work in the conversation without inventing completed content.

screens.name: Dashboard directory
screens.layout: Persistent workspace navigation frames a main dashboard directory. View tabs sit above a list with dashboard names and a separate owner column; creation appears in the upper corner. The directory emphasizes identity and ownership rather than miniature charts.
screens.lesson: Treat a dashboard directory as navigation before turning it into another dashboard.

screens.name: Issue performance dashboard
screens.layout: A page title, description area and filter controls lead into panels of unequal informational roles. A large headline count sits beside a scatter plot, with a wider time-based chart below. Each panel uses its own clear title and plotting area.
screens.lesson: Choose panel geometry from the information being conveyed instead of forcing equal cards.

screens.name: Issue distribution analytics
screens.layout: A large bar chart occupies the upper analysis area, with a detailed tabular breakdown beneath it. A narrow right-side control region holds metric and grouping choices, and a summary value remains near the chart controls. The view combines overview and exact comparison.
screens.lesson: Pair aggregate graphics with a precise data representation for inspection.

screens.name: Cycle history overview
screens.layout: The cycle list contains distinct upcoming, current and completed entries. The expanded current cycle shows a progress graph and adjacent summary values, while neighboring cycles retain compact headers and capacity information. Expansion changes detail density without replacing the list.
screens.lesson: Let the active period expand while keeping surrounding periods available for context.

screens.name: Desktop priority inbox
screens.layout: A compact Inbox heading precedes Priority and Other tabs with counts. Notification rows use avatars or object symbols, titles and smaller supporting text, with time and read-state cues aligned toward the right. The content remains a quiet, dense vertical list.
screens.lesson: Use tabs and row metadata to support triage without adding large notification cards.

screens.name: Inbox display options
screens.layout: An anchored settings panel opens over the inbox and selected issue. It groups priority inclusion and badge-count choices above unread grouping and ordering, followed by visibility toggles. Current values align consistently across the panel's rows.
screens.lesson: Keep view-specific configuration close to the view it modifies.

screens.name: Project specification document
screens.layout: A project breadcrumb and compact utility controls frame a narrow document column. An icon and title precede a summary, then section headings and paragraphs with a clear editorial rhythm. The document surface uses text hierarchy rather than nested cards.
screens.lesson: Use a calm reading column for long project reasoning inside a dense product shell.

screens.name: Project update feed entry
screens.layout: Feed navigation and a subscription action frame a dated update. Project identity, health and author metadata precede several paragraphs, with response controls below the text. The date sits in a separate leading position while the narrative stays in a consistent column.
screens.lesson: Keep chronological context distinct from the body of a progress update.

screens.name: Custom issue view editor
screens.layout: A named view and description sit above a row of active filter chips and matching/display controls. Grouped issue results occupy the main region, while view properties appear at the side and save/cancel actions remain near the top. Configuration and its result are visible together.
screens.lesson: Show the consequence of filtering in the same workspace where the filter is defined.

screens.name: Saved view destination picker
screens.layout: The custom-view editor remains visible while a Save to menu offers personal, workspace and team destinations. A check marks the current selection and the primary save action stays adjacent. The open menu describes visibility through concrete destination choices.
screens.lesson: Make the storage or sharing scope explicit at the moment a reusable view is saved.

screens.name: Service launcher
screens.layout: A centered welcome heading and short instruction introduce a grid of service destinations. Each destination pairs a large app symbol with a short label below it. Small novelty badges attach to selected icons, while generous space keeps the choices visually independent.
screens.lesson: Use recognizable symbols with persistent labels for service switching, and reserve badges for information that changes the selection decision.

screens.name: Plan comparison dialog
screens.layout: A dialog title sits above audience tabs and billing controls. Three adjacent plan columns repeat the same hierarchy: name, short description, prominent price, selection action, and feature rows. The middle option carries a recommendation badge and stronger outline; a close control occupies the corner.
screens.lesson: Keep prices and primary actions aligned across plans, and distinguish recommendations without breaking the shared comparison structure.

screens.name: Subscription review and payment
screens.layout: The review dialog divides into a wide configuration column and a narrower summary panel. An optional add-on precedes stacked billing-period choices, with payment details below. The summary groups plan identity, adjustments, total due, confirmation, and explanatory notes; a back control remains separate at the bottom.
screens.lesson: Place the final amount beside confirmation while retaining enough configuration context for users to understand what they are buying.

screens.name: Subscription settings and cancellation entry
screens.layout: A settings navigation rail remains visible beside a scrolled content area. Product update preferences form a dense vertical group of labeled toggles. Farther down, a separately titled cancellation section uses explanatory copy and one continuation button inside its own container, creating a break from routine preferences.
screens.lesson: Separate consequential account actions from routine preferences with their own heading, explanation, and deliberate action placement.

screens.name: Subscription cancellation review
screens.layout: A large centered cancellation heading spans two content columns. The first lists account benefits as repeated icon-and-text rows; the second presents supporting organizational information with linked image stories. Paired keep and cancel actions appear together beneath both columns, after the supporting material.
screens.lesson: When presenting a consequential choice, keep both outcomes visible together and avoid making explanatory content obscure the requested action.

screens.name: Mailbox with quick settings panel
screens.layout: The mailbox shell places folders and compose at the left, an empty message area in the center, and a settings inspector on the right. The inspector groups navigation shortcuts, compact preference rows, switches, and theme thumbnails beneath a clear title and close control.
screens.lesson: Use a contextual settings inspector for frequently adjusted preferences, while giving the full settings destination a clear place at the top.

screens.name: Subscription without saved payment methods
screens.layout: Account navigation frames a main column of subscription sections. A compact current-plan card appears first, followed by a payment-method card with explanatory copy, two add-method buttons, and an explicit absence message. A credits heading begins the next section below the payment group.
screens.lesson: Pair an empty payment state with available setup actions, keeping account status and optional credits in separate groups.

screens.name: Add card dialog
screens.layout: A compact card-entry dialog sits over the dimmed subscription page. Its fields group the card number with expiry and verification details, then country with postal code. An automatic-payment switch follows the address group, and cancel and save actions share the final row beneath the form.
screens.lesson: Group payment inputs by familiar card and address relationships, and keep optional authorization separate from the credentials themselves.

screens.name: Card verification explanation
screens.layout: A small verification dialog is layered above a subdued card form and account page. Its title leads into two short explanatory paragraphs about the bank check. The footer presents a secondary cancel action on one side and a prominent verification action on the other.
screens.lesson: Explain an external verification step before its action, using concise paragraphs and an obvious way to return to the form.

screens.name: Saved payment method list
screens.layout: The account sidebar anchors a subscription page with a current-plan card above a payment-method section. Within that section, setup buttons precede a compact table of method, status, and actions. The saved card occupies one row with a default badge and trailing edit menu.
screens.lesson: Expose payment status in the same row as the method, and keep editing actions consistently aligned at the table edge.

screens.name: Add external payment provider
screens.layout: A narrow centered dialog overlays the subscription settings page. A short heading precedes explanatory paragraphs describing provider requirements and the next step. Two stacked actions conclude the dialog: a provider-branded action followed by cancel, both aligned to the same content width.
screens.lesson: For payment-provider handoffs, put prerequisites before the external action and offer a nearby, clearly labeled return path.

screens.name: Payment method actions menu
screens.layout: The payment section shows two saved methods in aligned rows with a default marker attached to one. A small menu opens from the other row’s trailing control, containing a default-setting action and a separated deletion option. The credits card remains visible beneath this table.
screens.lesson: Attach method actions to their specific row, and distinguish destructive operations from changes to the preferred payment option.

screens.name: Delete payment method confirmation
screens.layout: A compact confirmation dialog sits over a dimmed payment-method table. The title names the object being removed, followed by a service-continuity explanation and a direct confirmation question. A strong delete action and a quieter cancel action stack below the message.
screens.lesson: Name the affected object and describe the practical consequence before a destructive action, keeping cancellation equally easy to locate.

screens.name: Diff display preferences
screens.layout: The changed-files workspace retains its navigation tabs, file tree, and code area while a display-options popover occupies the toolbar vicinity. Illustrated unified and split choices sit side by side above a whitespace checkbox. A single apply action concludes the compact settings group.
screens.lesson: Use small structural previews when view modes differ visually, and keep their controls adjacent to the content they affect.

screens.name: Inline review comment composer
screens.layout: A bordered comment composer begins with write and preview tabs alongside formatting tools. A large empty text field dominates the panel. Attachment guidance sits below on the left, while cancel, comment, and review-start actions form a compact group at the lower right.
screens.lesson: Give authored content the largest area, and group submission options together without letting formatting tools dominate the composer.

screens.name: Image file review panel
screens.layout: A file header combines a disclosure control, file metadata, path, and trailing review controls. Beneath it, a broad preview region centers the image with substantial surrounding space. The comment control stays in the header, visually tied to the reviewed file rather than the image content.
screens.lesson: Anchor review tools to the file container so large previews remain unobstructed while file identity and comment scope stay clear.

screens.name: Finish code review panel
screens.layout: A review panel combines a titled header with a comment editor and formatting toolbar. Beneath the editor, three radio choices pair outcome labels with short explanations. A pending-comments disclosure precedes a separated footer containing discard on the left and cancel plus submit on the right.
screens.lesson: Separate review content from review outcome, and explain each outcome beside its selection control before the final submission action.

screens.name: Review conversation navigator
screens.layout: A conversations popover appears above the code diff beneath the review toolbar. An unresolved section contains author avatars, names, age metadata, comment excerpts, and file context. A compact outdated badge distinguishes one item, while a resolved section forms a separate row at the bottom.
screens.lesson: Group discussion navigation by resolution state and preserve author, excerpt, and file context so similar threads remain distinguishable.

screens.name: Files table workspace
screens.layout: A global app bar spans the workspace above a left navigation rail and file table. Search and file-scope destinations occupy the rail; the main toolbar holds creation and view controls. Rows align selection, file identity, sharing indicators, actions, size, and modification information, with a summary underneath.
screens.lesson: Keep file identity dominant while aligning metadata and row actions predictably, and separate workspace navigation from collection controls.

screens.name: File actions in context
screens.layout: The file workspace retains its navigation rail and aligned table while a menu is anchored beside a folder’s action control. The menu stacks icon-labeled operations for organization, movement, reminders, local access, and download. A divider separates deletion at the bottom from the routine file actions.
screens.lesson: Keep file menus attached to their row and order operations in recognizable groups, isolating deletion from everyday organization tasks.

screens.name: File sharing inspector
screens.layout: A selected file remains visible in the central table while a right inspector presents its name and metadata. Sharing, activity, and version tabs sit below the identity block. The active sharing section separates internal recipients, existing access, internal links, and external sharing controls into distinct groups.
screens.lesson: Preserve the selected file’s context while separating internal access from external sharing so each permission decision has an explicit scope.

screens.name: Folder activity inspector
screens.layout: The file table and navigation remain alongside a right inspector titled with the folder name. A small metadata line precedes sharing and activity tabs. The active activity area places a comment field above a chronological sequence of compact events with actor or action symbols and relative timestamps.
screens.lesson: Combine activity and a concise comment entry point in one inspector while keeping object identity visible above the event history.

screens.name: Filtered file search
screens.layout: A query appears in the navigation search field, while the main workspace shows a related query chip beside a scope action. The standard file-table columns remain in place around a single folder result. A result count sits immediately beneath the row, with open space below.
screens.lesson: Keep the active query and its scope visible near results, retaining familiar row anatomy even when very few matches remain.

screens.name: Files thumbnail grid
screens.layout: The file workspace combines its standard navigation rail with a main thumbnail grid. Folder symbols, document symbols, and image previews share a common tile structure. Each item has a selection box above, a name and time below, and a trailing menu; a collection summary follows the tiles.
screens.lesson: Use previews to support recognition while keeping selection, labels, metadata, and actions in consistent positions across mixed file types.

screens.name: Create and upload file menu
screens.layout: A menu attached to the main creation button overlays the top of the file table. Its first labeled group contains upload actions for files and folders. A separator introduces a second group for new folders, file requests, and templates, while the surrounding navigation and table retain context.
screens.lesson: Distinguish importing existing material from creating new material with labeled menu groups rather than presenting one undifferentiated action list.

screens.name: Bulk file selection
screens.layout: Three selected file rows show checked boxes beneath the normal workspace toolbar. A contextual line above the rows replaces ordinary column emphasis with the selected count and bulk actions.
