Unselected rows retain empty boxes, and the navigation rail plus file metadata remain unchanged around the selection.
screens.lesson: Make selection scope explicit with both row markers and a count, placing batch actions close to the selected collection.

screens.name: Public folder permission options
screens.layout: A sharing inspector displays its active tab, recipient entry field, and a list of access routes. A popover anchored to the public-link row contains mutually exclusive access modes followed by independent restriction checkboxes. Removal and additional-link actions occupy the bottom of the menu.
screens.lesson: Separate exclusive access modes from additive restrictions, and tie their controls visibly to the specific share link being configured.

screens.name: Recipient permission checklist
screens.layout: A recipient search field tops a sharing panel with public-link and named-recipient rows. The named recipient’s menu exposes a vertical permission checklist, followed by an expiration date field and optional note setting. Related resources remain behind the menu, and unsharing appears at its bottom.
screens.lesson: Attach granular permissions to a named recipient and keep time limits beside those permissions so the access grant reads as one decision.

screens.name: Incoming share notification
screens.layout: A notification panel is attached beneath the application’s notification area. Relative time and a dismiss control appear above a share symbol, folder name, and sender identity. Reject and accept actions align together at the lower edge, making the requested decision part of the same compact unit.
screens.lesson: Put the shared object and sender before invitation actions, and distinguish dismissing a notification from deciding on the invitation.

screens.name: Access membership and origin
screens.layout: The sharing panel places a recipient field above link controls and an expanded access list. Avatars distinguish groups, shared links, and individual people in repeated rows. A person-specific popover adds who granted access and through which folder, with a separate unshare action beneath those details.
screens.lesson: Show where inherited or delegated access originates before offering removal, helping users understand the relationship behind a permission entry.

screens.name: Add a shared folder to an account
screens.layout: A compact menu beneath a download control presents a direct-link field in its first group. A second group identifies the add-to-account action and includes a server or account address field with an arrow action at its trailing edge. Labels and icons distinguish the two destinations.
screens.lesson: Keep a transfer destination field inside its named action group, and distinguish copying a link from adding content to another account.

screens.name: Files connection settings
screens.layout: A files-settings dialog uses a category list on the left and configuration content on the right. Warning switches remain visible above the WebDAV section. That section groups a labeled connection address with a copy control, followed by a separately styled help link with an external-link symbol.
screens.lesson: Group connection information with its copy action and place explanatory help nearby, while retaining clear settings-category navigation.

screens.name: Connect to a file server
screens.layout: A file manager remains visible behind a server-connection dialog and open application menu. The dialog groups a labeled server-address field with an example below, then an empty recent-servers list. Browse sits at the lower left, while cancel and connect appear together at the lower right.
screens.lesson: Present the connection address first, keep prior destinations distinct, and separate browsing for a server from confirming a typed destination.

screens.name: Connect to server dialog
screens.layout: A standalone server-connection dialog begins with a labeled address field and adjacent controls for saved entries. A favorite-servers list occupies the middle beneath its heading. Help and remove controls sit below the list, while browse and connect actions align together at the opposite edge.
screens.lesson: Keep typed destinations separate from saved favorites, and give the final connection action a stable place beside secondary browsing.

screens.name: Map a network drive
screens.layout: A network-drive wizard introduces the task with a question and short instruction. A drive selector and folder-address field form aligned labeled rows, with browse beside the address. Reconnection and credential checkboxes follow, then a help link; finish and cancel occupy a separated bottom action strip.
screens.lesson: Lead connection setup with the destination, then group persistence and credential options beneath it before the final confirmation controls.

screens.name: Create a vault item or collection
screens.layout: The vault workspace shows navigation at the left, a filter column, and a table of saved items. An open menu under the new-item button lists credential types first, followed by folder and collection destinations after a separator. The table preserves item identity and ownership information behind the menu.
screens.lesson: Group creation options by object type and organizational structure, keeping the menu beside the collection it will affect.

screens.name: Assign selected vault items
screens.layout: A vault table sits beside application navigation and a filter column. Several item rows are selected, with checked boxes and a shared row treatment. A compact action bar at the bottom states the count and groups clear, folder assignment, collection assignment, and additional actions beneath the selected items.
screens.lesson: Use a count-bearing action bar for bulk operations, and keep destination changes visibly tied to the current selection.

screens.name: Organization collection bulk controls
screens.layout: An administration sidebar and item-type filters frame an organization collection table. Selected rows retain item names, collection badges, and permission text in aligned columns. A bottom action bar combines the selection count with clear, collection assignment, archive, and delete actions, directly below the listed records.
screens.lesson: Preserve collection and permission metadata during bulk selection so administrators can assess scope before applying changes to multiple records.

screens.name: Vault ownership fields
screens.layout: An edit dialog overlays the vault list, with a clear title and close control above the item-details group. A full-width name field precedes side-by-side owner and folder selectors. A required collections field spans the row below, and the credentials section begins at the lower crop edge.
screens.lesson: Group ownership and collection membership near item identity, making access-related placement distinct from the credentials that follow.

screens.name: Desktop vault selection
screens.layout: A desktop vault window places category navigation beside a searchable item table. Selected entries appear among unselected rows with names, supporting account text, owner badges, and trailing actions. A bottom selection bar combines the count with clear, folder, collection, and overflow controls, separated from the individual row actions.
screens.lesson: Keep batch controls visually separate from row controls and retain ownership information while users choose records for a shared operation.

screens.name: Desktop vault item editor
screens.layout: A desktop window divides into a navigation rail, a searchable vault list, and an item editor. The editor groups name, owner, collections, and folder before a credentials section. Save and cancel controls sit at the bottom, while the selected item remains identifiable in the neighboring list.
screens.lesson: Keep the source list visible beside item editing, and order identity, ownership, and credentials into clear groups within the inspector.

screens.name: Vault sharing action menu
screens.layout: The vault interface presents navigation, filters, and an item table in adjacent columns. An action menu opens from one record’s trailing control, stacking editing, attachments, copying, collection assignment, sharing, archiving, and deletion choices. The selected record’s name and owner remain visible beside the menu.
screens.lesson: Anchor sharing actions to the item row and retain identity nearby so users can confirm the object before choosing an access operation.

screens.name: Share a vault item
screens.layout: A share dialog starts with a compact item-identity card. The next group contains recipient emails, explanatory text, an expiration selector, and a one-time-share checkbox. Existing links appear below in repeated rows with expiry information and trailing controls; copy and cancel actions form the footer.
screens.lesson: Place recipient and duration controls before existing links, and retain item identity so link creation has an unmistakable scope.

screens.name: Shared item email verification error
screens.layout: A centered illustration and verification heading lead into a single-field form card. The required email input shows a visible validation message beneath it, followed by a subdued send-code button. A short product explanation with links sits outside the card below the form.
screens.lesson: Place field errors directly beside the affected input, and distinguish task completion controls from secondary explanatory or promotional links.

screens.name: Shared credential detail
screens.layout: A compact recipient view begins with a shared-item illustration, heading, and sender statement. An item-identity card precedes a credentials group containing username and masked password rows with trailing copy or visibility controls. Expiration information sits separately beneath the content, completing the reading sequence.
screens.lesson: Establish item identity before exposing sensitive fields, keep per-field actions adjacent, and state access duration outside the credential values.

screens.name: Master password security settings
screens.layout: Account navigation sits beside a security page with horizontal subsection tabs. The active password section begins with a warning callout, then stacks current password, new password, confirmation, and hint fields. Supporting guidance and password options appear below relevant inputs, with the final action at the form’s end.
screens.lesson: Put security consequences before password fields, keep guidance close to its input, and separate optional account changes from the core update.

screens.name: Desktop account menu
screens.layout: A desktop vault window displays a category sidebar and searchable table of credentials with ownership labels and trailing row controls. The native account menu is open above the workspace, listing membership, password, two-step login, identity verification, and deletion entries independently from the table’s item-level actions.
screens.lesson: Keep account-wide security actions in a distinct menu so they cannot be confused with actions on an individual vault entry.

screens.name: Vault login method choice
screens.layout: A welcome heading and account identifier sit above a compact login card. The card presents a required master-password field, a nearby hint link, and the primary login button. A small alternative separator introduces device login, with a back action placed below both authentication choices.
screens.lesson: Keep alternative authentication methods within the same task card while distinguishing them from password recovery and backward navigation.

screens.name: Recovery code dialog
screens.layout: A recovery-code dialog overlays part of the two-step-login settings page. Its header names the code type and provides a close control. The body centers a short explanation above the grouped code, while a separated footer places print and close actions together beneath the sensitive content.
screens.lesson: Give recovery material a focused container with a clear label, a deliberate export action, and an obvious exit path.

screens.name: Settings search results
screens.layout: A query field spans the top of the settings pane, with a result count at its trailing edge. Scope tabs sit beneath it. An indented category tree occupies the left column, while the wider results column stacks named settings, explanatory copy, and their associated controls.
screens.lesson: Keep search scope, category counts, and result controls visible together so a filtered configuration remains understandable as a collection.

screens.name: Appearance settings with modified markers
screens.layout: The settings pane places search and scope controls above a two-column body. An expanded Workbench branch identifies Appearance in the left tree. The content column stacks appearance fields, each with a title, explanation, and selector. Narrow vertical markers accompany changed rows, with one row visibly outlined.
screens.lesson: Place change indicators beside the affected setting, while retaining the category hierarchy and enough explanation to interpret each current value.

screens.name: Setting actions menu
screens.layout: A setting row is outlined in the main content column beneath the search field and scope tabs. A gear beside its label anchors an open menu. The menu groups reset, copy, profile, and synchronization commands with separators while the category navigation remains visible to the left.
screens.lesson: Anchor secondary actions to the setting they affect, and group commands by purpose so the field itself keeps a clear identity.

screens.name: Source control preferences
screens.layout: A wide search field and scope tabs lead the pane. The left navigation expands Features into a long list of categories, with Source Control selected. The adjacent content begins with the matching heading and presents a vertical sequence of named preferences, explanatory sentences, checkboxes, and a selector.
screens.lesson: Repeat the selected navigation label as the content heading, then give each preference a consistent label, explanation, and control order.

screens.name: Modified settings filter
screens.layout: The search field contains a modified-settings token and a result count. Scope tabs separate that filter from the body. Category branches on the left show counts, while the results column combines changed-value markers, labels, explanatory text, checkboxes, and selectors. A highlighted row includes an adjacent gear action.
screens.lesson: Pair an explicit filter token with category counts and per-row markers to make a collection of changed values easy to scan.

screens.name: Settings filter suggestions
screens.layout: A suggestion list opens directly beneath the settings search field and overlaps the settings body. Each row contains a filter token, with the first row visibly selected. The underlying scope tabs and part of an individual setting remain visible, placing the suggestion list within the configuration workspace.
screens.lesson: Keep filter suggestions attached to the query field, using consistent token syntax and a clear selected row without losing the surrounding task.

screens.name: Extension preferences category
screens.layout: The upper portion contains a search field and scope tabs. The left tree expands Extensions into a list of installed tools and selects C/C++. The main column repeats that category as a heading, then groups named options with explanatory copy, checkboxes, and a dropdown aligned beneath their labels.
screens.lesson: Use the same navigation and field anatomy for extension preferences as built-in settings, while clearly identifying the extension currently being configured.

screens.name: Extension feature contribution details
screens.layout: An extension identity block combines an icon, name, version, publisher, usage metadata, rating, summary, and management actions. A tab strip divides the information below. The selected Feature Contributions tab shows an expandable Settings section containing aligned columns for setting names, descriptions, and default values.
screens.lesson: Place extension identity and management actions above technical tables, and align descriptive fields so users can compare contributions without losing context.

screens.name: Settings JSON completion with explanation
screens.layout: A file tab and breadcrumb path identify the settings document above a numbered code editor. A partially entered property has a suggestion list immediately below it. The selected suggestion is paired with an adjacent description panel, while preceding configuration lines remain visible above the completion overlay.
screens.lesson: Keep completion choices close to the insertion point and give the selected choice adjacent explanation without replacing the surrounding code context.

screens.name: Workspace settings file in Explorer
screens.layout: A vertical activity rail borders a file explorer on the left, and a code editor occupies the right. The explorer expands the project and its configuration folder, highlighting settings.json. The editor repeats the filename in its tab and breadcrumb, then shows a compact numbered configuration document.
screens.lesson: Reinforce the selected file across navigation, tab, and breadcrumb so project-specific configuration remains distinguishable from other settings documents.

screens.name: Language settings beside JSON
screens.layout: Two adjacent editor panes show a settings form and a JSON document. The left pane includes a language filter, scoped tabs, and a vertical stack of options. The right pane shows numbered code with a language-specific block and selected property, aligned beside the corresponding form setting.
screens.lesson: When exposing both structured and textual configuration, preserve scope labels and recognizable property names so the two representations can be compared.

screens.name: Language selection palette
screens.layout: A floating selection surface sits near the top of an otherwise empty editor window. Its input field leads a vertical language list, with one row selected. Each option includes a language name and a secondary identifier. The application title bar and bottom status bar frame the surrounding workspace.
screens.lesson: Use secondary identifiers to distinguish similar language options, keeping the query and selected row prominent within a compact chooser.

screens.name: Language-scoped preferences
screens.layout: The settings query includes a language token, and both scope tabs explicitly name that language. A counted category tree sits on the left. The content column presents diff-editor preferences with checkboxes, numeric inputs, descriptions, and a highlighted row, all beneath the persistent search and scope region.
screens.lesson: Restate active scope in more than one relevant location when a preference can differ across languages or workspaces.

screens.name: Account menu with synchronization action
screens.layout: An account icon on the activity rail anchors an open menu near the bottom of the workspace. A status line states that no account is signed in. Three separated action rows follow, with Backup and Sync Settings selected. The application status bar remains visible beneath the menu.
screens.lesson: Explain account status before account-dependent commands, and make the current menu choice distinct without obscuring the persistent navigation anchor.

screens.name: Experimental settings filter
screens.layout: A settings search field contains an experimental tag and shows a result count. Scope tabs and a synchronization action form the next row. The category tree selects an extension branch, while the results column shows settings with long hierarchical labels, explanatory copy, and explicit Experimental badges.
screens.lesson: Label experimental options at the field level as well as in the filter, preserving that qualification when users scan individual results.

screens.name: Explorer beside empty editor
screens.layout: The window has a compact title toolbar, an activity rail on the far left, and a file explorer beside a large unoccupied editor region. The explorer lists one project, a folder, and files with status markers. Collapsed Outline and Timeline sections sit below the tree, above the full-width status bar.
screens.lesson: Keep project navigation useful when no document is open, and reserve the dominant area for working content rather than expanding secondary sections.

screens.name: Explorer and assistant sidebars
screens.layout: A large empty editor region is bordered by a project explorer on the left and a conversation panel on the right. The explorer lists files and collapsed secondary sections. The conversation panel contains a question, response text, reference metadata, and a bottom composer with compact attachment and model controls.
screens.lesson: Give navigation and conversation separate edges around the workspace, and keep the composer anchored within the conversation rather than across unrelated content.

screens.name: Centered layout customization menu
screens.layout: A floating Customize Layout surface occupies the middle of an empty editor window. A title row contains reset and close controls. The visible list is divided into alignment, quick-input position, and display-mode groups, with category labels at the right, selected-state checks, icons, and shortcuts on applicable rows.
screens.lesson: Group layout options by the part of the workspace they affect, and show current choices alongside familiar position labels.

screens.name: Activity rail size submenu
screens.layout: An activity-rail context menu lists workspace destinations with checkmarks and right-aligned shortcuts. A separator introduces account and positioning options below. The selected Activity Bar Size row opens a smaller submenu to the right containing two choices, one checked, while the rail and status bar remain partially visible.
screens.lesson: Separate destination visibility from layout configuration, and align a short submenu with its parent row to preserve a clear choice hierarchy.

screens.name: Workspace layout options
screens.layout: The Customize Layout surface opens from the upper toolbar. It stacks groups for region visibility, primary sidebar placement, panel alignment, and display modes. Icons precede option labels; group captions occupy the right edge. Checks identify selected positions, and reset and close controls share the surface header.
screens.lesson: Collect related layout controls in one grouped surface, using positional vocabulary and selection marks to describe the current arrangement clearly.

screens.name: Terminal panel position submenu
screens.layout: A terminal panel shows its tab strip across the top, a prompt in the body, and a terminal-session list at the right. A context menu overlays the panel and lists available views. The Panel Position row opens a directional submenu, with the current bottom position checked.
screens.lesson: Place panel configuration within the panel context, and retain view labels and current position marks so layout choices remain grounded.

screens.name: Problems sidebar with source control panel
screens.layout: A diagnostics list occupies the left sidebar beside a code document. Its filter field and grouped issue rows show icons, messages, and line references. Beneath the editor, a Source Control panel contains a commit-message field, prominent Commit action, and a changes list. Tabs identify neighboring lower-panel tools.
screens.lesson: Assign persistent regions to diagnostics and change management while protecting an uninterrupted code area and keeping each panel’s local actions together.

screens.name: Explorer output and problems layout
screens.layout: The left sidebar stacks a project tree above an Output section with a source selector and log text. A document editor fills the upper-right region, including tabs and breadcrumbs. The lower-right panel lists diagnostics with severity icons and line references under a toolbar and filter field.
screens.lesson: Use independently headed sections when combining navigation and logs, keeping diagnostic lists adjacent to the document they help explain.

screens.name: Grouped file search results
screens.layout: A Search heading and compact toolbar sit above a query field. A summary line reports results and offers an editor link. Below, a folder and file hierarchy groups matching snippets. Occurrences are visibly marked within each snippet, and count badges align near the trailing edge of grouped rows.
screens.lesson: Group text matches under their files and preserve a brief results summary so repeated snippets remain navigable without losing their source identity.

screens.name: Search toolbar customization menu
screens.layout: A search panel remains visible behind an open toolbar menu. The panel includes a query, results summary, and grouped matching snippets. The overlay lists search commands and view options, using checks for visible commands, separators between groups, and a selected reset command at the bottom.
screens.lesson: Expose toolbar customization beside the affected controls, and use checked entries and a distinct reset command to make the configuration legible.

screens.name: Editor tab split and move menu
screens.layout: A menu opens below an editor tab over the code surface. It groups closing commands, path-copy actions, file actions, pinning, and splitting with separators. The selected Split and Move row opens a second column of directional split and move choices, followed by a separate within-group split command.
screens.lesson: Group tab commands by intent and place directional variants in a submenu, keeping the primary menu readable despite many document actions.

screens.name: Four-region editor workspace
screens.layout: The working area is divided into four adjoining panes. Markdown source and a rendered preview occupy the upper pair, while keyboard shortcuts and another document occupy the lower pair. Each region has its own tab or heading controls, and strong intersecting dividers make the pane boundaries explicit.
screens.lesson: Give each region independent identity and local controls in dense workspaces, and make split boundaries clear enough to preserve content ownership.

screens.name: Editor group actions menu
screens.layout: An editor group shows several tabs, breadcrumbs, and a numbered document. A menu opens from the group toolbar at the upper right. It separates open-editor navigation, close commands, a checked preview preference, and the selected Lock Group command, retaining the underlying group header and document context.
screens.lesson: Place group-wide actions in the group header and separate navigation, closing, and persistence controls so their scopes are easy to distinguish.

screens.name: Automatic editor group locking preferences
screens.layout: A settings search field contains a precise property name and a single-result count. Scope tabs and a synchronization action precede the body. A narrow category column sits beside one long setting explanation and a vertical checklist of editor types, where a terminal option is visibly checked.
screens.lesson: Use a checklist for independently configurable content types, and keep the shared rule explanation above the list rather than repeating it per item.

screens.name: Annotated editor workspace overview
screens.layout: A file tree and activity rail occupy the left edge of the application. Two code panes share the upper working area, while a terminal spans beneath them. Tabs identify documents, and a status bar closes the window. External labels and brackets identify these major interface regions around the screenshot.
screens.lesson: Establish a stable division between navigation, documents, and supporting tools, and preserve each region’s identity when showing several kinds of work together.

screens.name: Three adjacent editor groups
screens.layout: Three vertical editor groups sit beside an activity rail. The first two contain numbered code documents, while the third presents rendered Markdown with a heading, links, badges, and an embedded image. Each group has its own tab row, with breadcrumbs visible above the code columns.
screens.lesson: Use independent document headers across parallel panes, allowing different content representations to coexist while keeping the reading order within each pane clear.

screens.name: Notebook and floating data window
screens.layout: The desktop shows a primary editor window behind a smaller overlapping data window. The main window contains a file tree, notebook title, introductory prose, code cell, and a partial table. The foreground window presents a CSV document with its own title bar, tab, numbered rows, and minimap.
screens.lesson: Preserve document identity in detached windows so supporting data can remain visible alongside a larger analytical workspace without relying on shared tabs.

screens.name: Code editor with document minimap
screens.layout: A code document fills the pane under a file tab and breadcrumb path. Line numbers and indentation guides structure the main text. A narrow minimap occupies the right edge and includes compact section labels. A marked code region and gutter hint sit within the larger numbered document.
screens.lesson: Keep a document overview at the edge of the editor and use structural landmarks to orient readers without interrupting the primary code column.

screens.name: Nested project files and empty workspace
screens.layout: A vertical activity rail borders a file explorer containing expanded project files. A package manifest nests its related lockfile beneath it. The large editor area contains a central emblem and a short list of command hints with shortcuts. A title toolbar and status bar frame the workspace.
screens.lesson: Use nesting to clarify relationships among companion files, while an empty working area can offer a compact set of relevant starting commands.

screens.name: Explorer filename filter
screens.layout: A project explorer places an inline filter field beneath the project heading. Compact filter-mode controls and a close icon follow the query. Folder branches contain matching filenames, with the matching substring marked in both folder and file labels. One result row is selected within the visible hierarchy.
screens.lesson: Preserve folder relationships while filtering filenames, and mark the matching substring so the reason each result appears remains visible.

screens.name: Code outline with sorting menu
screens.layout: An Outline panel sits beside a numbered code document. A filter field leads an indented list of symbols, each with a type icon and nested members. An open menu overlays the boundary between outline and code, showing cursor-following, filtering, and sorting choices with checks beside active options.
screens.lesson: Place outline controls near the symbol tree, and keep symbol type and nesting visible so structural navigation remains useful beside the source.

screens.name: Markdown document outline
screens.layout: A compact Outline panel has a heading toolbar and a filter field above a nested heading list. Rows use indentation, disclosure arrows, text-symbol icons, and heading markers to express hierarchy. A selected section sits among its parent and child headings, with small indicators at some trailing row edges.
screens.lesson: Use indentation and heading-level markers together in document outlines, keeping the selected section visible among its neighboring hierarchy.

screens.name: File history timeline panel
screens.layout: The explorer sidebar stacks collapsed Open Editors, project, and Outline sections above an expanded Timeline. The timeline heading names its file. Rows pair a small history marker with a change description and author text, while relative times align at the right. The activity rail remains visible alongside.
screens.lesson: Keep file identity in the timeline heading and align timestamps consistently so history can be scanned without separating events from their document.

screens.name: File command palette
screens.layout: A floating command palette sits below the window toolbar, beside the visible activity rail. A query field spans its top. The list beneath contains file-related commands, with one selected row, a trailing configuration icon, and shortcuts aligned on applicable rows. The surrounding editor remains visually subordinate.
screens.lesson: Give the command input a clear lead position and reserve a consistent trailing area for shortcuts and selected-command actions.

screens.name: Quick navigation help palette
screens.layout: A floating quick-input surface contains a question-mark query followed by navigation choices. Each row pairs a short query prefix with an explanation such as file, line, or symbol navigation. Several rows show right-aligned keyboard shortcuts. One option is selected, and the application activity rail remains visible behind it.
screens.lesson: Present query syntax beside plain-language meanings, making advanced navigation discoverable within the same surface where users enter commands.

screens.name: Commonly used settings
screens.layout: A search field stretches across the settings pane. Scope tabs and a synchronization action sit below it, above a two-column body. The left column lists setting categories; the right begins with Commonly Used and stacks an autosave selector, numeric font-size field, and font-family field with persistent labels and explanations.
screens.lesson: Combine category navigation with a concise common-settings section, keeping scope controls above both navigation and fields for consistent orientation.

screens.name: Notification with response actions
screens.layout: A compact notification panel contains a title row with several utility controls. Its single notification pairs an information icon with a short message and a source label below. Response buttons sit at the lower right of the item, with settings and dismissal controls near its upper edge.
screens.lesson: Keep message identity, source, and response actions within one notification unit, while separating item controls from panel-level utilities.

screens.name: Tabbed code editor and open files
screens.layout: The left sidebar shows an Open Editors list above the project file tree, with Outline and Timeline collapsed below. The main pane has several document tabs, a breadcrumb row, and a numbered code editor. The selected file is repeated across the open-file list, tree, and active tab.
screens.lesson: Repeat document identity consistently across open-file lists and tabs, while keeping project structure separate from the temporary set of open work.

screens.name: Custom tab label pattern form
screens.layout: A filtered settings pane shows one checkbox preference followed by a larger custom-label pattern setting. The second setting includes explanatory paragraphs, variable examples, and a compact key-value editing row. Item and Value headers align above the two inputs, with confirmation and cancellation controls at the row’s trailing edge.
screens.lesson: Place syntax help immediately above a compact pattern editor, and keep row-level confirmation adjacent to the values being changed.

screens.name: Editor grid with empty group
screens.layout: The editor window divides its workspace into four rectangular groups. Two code documents occupy the left column, an untitled document occupies the upper right, and an empty group fills the lower right. Tabs and local controls identify occupied groups. An explanatory arrow and label point to the empty group.
screens.lesson: Maintain visible boundaries and headers for empty regions in a multi-pane workspace so unoccupied space still has an understandable role.

screens.name: Editor layout menu
screens.layout: The View menu opens from the application menu bar over an empty editor. Its Editor Layout row expands a second menu to the right. The submenu groups directional splitting, window movement, and named column or row arrangements, with separators and shortcuts distinguishing individual operations from layout presets.
screens.lesson: Separate layout presets from individual split commands so users can choose between arranging the whole workspace and changing one editor region.

screens.name: Explorer section visibility menu
screens.layout: A project explorer shows folders and files beside the activity rail. Its header overflow control anchors a short menu. The menu lists Open Editors, Folders, Outline, Timeline, and NPM Scripts, with checkmarks beside visible sections and a selected row at the top. The file hierarchy remains visible behind it.
screens.lesson: Attach section-visibility choices to the containing pane’s header, and use checkmarks so the menu communicates the current composition at a glance.

screens.name: General application preferences
screens.layout: A settings window places an icon-and-label category list on the left and a scrollable preferences area on the right. The content is divided into titled groups for general options, output, source alignment, projectors, and the system tray. Checkboxes and selectors align within each group, above bottom-right dialog actions.
screens.lesson: Use titled groups to make a dense preference dialog scannable, preserving a fixed category column and predictable confirmation area across sections.

screens.name: Stream service configuration
screens.layout: A settings window displays a vertical category list with Stream selected. The main area contains three compact rows for service, server, and stream key. The key field has adjacent Show and Get Stream Key controls. Generous unused space separates the configuration block from confirmation controls at the lower right.
screens.lesson: Group service identity and credentials together, and place credential-specific actions beside their field rather than in the global dialog footer.

screens.name: Streaming and recording output preferences
screens.layout: The Output category is selected in a left navigation column. A mode selector spans the top of the main pane. Separate Streaming and Recording groups contain labels, dropdowns, numeric values, a path field with Browse, and checkboxes. A warning line sits below these groups, above the bottom-right dialog actions.
screens.lesson: Divide output settings by destination and keep a consequence note near the relevant configuration rather than mixing it into navigation or actions.

screens.name: Video resolution configuration
screens.layout: The settings window selects Video in its left category list. The upper main area contains rows for canvas resolution, scaled output resolution, downscaling filter, and frame rate. Aspect-ratio annotations follow the resolution fields. Most of the lower area is unoccupied, with confirmation controls placed at the bottom right.
screens.lesson: Keep related numeric concepts in adjacent rows and put derived annotations beside their inputs so users can compare base and output configurations.

screens.name: Hotkey assignments
screens.layout: A Hotkeys category is selected beside a dense assignment list. A filter field leads the main pane. Each action label is paired with a long input and a repeated cluster of small row controls. A Scene heading separates a second group of assignments, and dialog actions remain at the lower right.
screens.lesson: Align repeated assignment inputs and row controls consistently, and divide global and object-specific shortcuts with headings so dense lists remain navigable.

screens.name: Advanced output and network preferences
screens.layout: A category sidebar selects Advanced beside a scrollable main pane. Titled groups separate general priority, video formatting, recording filenames, stream delay, reconnection, and network settings. Labels align beside inputs and dropdowns, with subordinate checkboxes beneath relevant values. A consistent action row sits at the lower-right edge.
screens.lesson: Break advanced settings into meaningful operational groups and place subordinate options beneath the values they qualify, preserving a stable alignment across groups.

screens.name: Source transform context menu
screens.layout: The lower studio workspace shows Scenes, Sources, Mixer, transitions, and broadcast controls in adjacent panels. A selected source anchors an open context menu. Its Transform row expands a submenu containing edit, reset, rotation, flipping, and fit commands, with shortcuts aligned at the right of selected entries.
screens.lesson: Keep object transformations attached to the selected source and group related geometry commands so a long command set remains grounded in context.

screens.name: Source filter configuration
screens.layout: A source-specific filter window divides its left column into Audio/Video Filters and Effect Filters lists, each with bottom controls. The selected effect appears in the lower list. A large preview occupies the upper-right region, with two property selectors beneath it and a Close action at the lower-right corner.
screens.lesson: Separate filter categories from the selected filter’s properties, and reserve a stable preview area to connect configuration with the source being edited.

screens.name: Studio preview and live composition
screens.layout: Two large previews occupy the top of the studio window, labeled Edit View and Live View. A narrow central strip contains transition controls. Along the bottom, adjacent panels hold scenes, sources, audio channels, transition settings, and broadcast actions. A small status strip runs beneath the panel row.
screens.lesson: Give preparation and live output equal visual identity, place transition controls between them, and keep supporting source and audio tools below the previews.

screens.name: Source visibility and locking panel
screens.layout: A Sources panel contains two rows beneath its heading. Source-type icons precede names, while visibility and lock icons align at the trailing edge. One source is dimmed and has a crossed-out visibility symbol. A compact footer groups addition, removal, settings, and ordering controls beneath the list.
screens.lesson: Align visibility and lock states per source, and keep list-wide creation and ordering controls in a separate footer to avoid crowding names.

screens.name: Selected window capture on studio canvas
screens.layout: A large selected capture fills most of the preview canvas beneath the menu bar. A bounding outline and handles frame the captured window. Below the preview, a source-property strip precedes adjacent panels for scenes, sources, audio mixing, transitions, and broadcast controls. Status information occupies the bottom edge.
screens.lesson: Keep selection boundaries visible on the canvas while preserving source identity and production controls in consistent supporting regions below it.

screens.name: Source transform precision dialog
screens.layout: A source-named transform dialog presents a vertically aligned form. Paired numeric fields describe position and size, with rotation between them. Alignment and bounding-box selectors follow, then paired crop controls for opposite edges. Some bounding-box fields are visibly unavailable. Reset and Close actions occupy opposite ends of the footer.
screens.lesson: Pair related geometric values spatially, group crop controls by edge, and distinguish unavailable fields without disrupting the form’s alignment.

screens.name: Cropped capture within studio canvas
screens.layout: A selected capture appears centered within a larger canvas, leaving open space on every side. Its boundary and handles identify the active source. A properties strip separates the canvas from the bottom row of scenes, sources, audio meters, transitions, and broadcast actions, with status information beneath.
screens.lesson: Preserve the surrounding canvas when showing a transformed source so its size and placement remain understandable relative to the output frame.

screens.name: Usage selection configuration wizard
screens.layout: The wizard begins with a Usage Information heading and a short instruction. Three radio options describe streaming, recording, and virtual-camera intentions, with the first selected. Explanatory copy sits below the choices. A footer separates Back, Next, and Cancel, with Back visibly unavailable in this captured step.
screens.lesson: Begin configuration with a small set of user intentions, then explain the consequence of that choice before the step navigation controls.

screens.name: Audio mixer channels
screens.layout: A narrow Audio Mixer panel stacks four channels under a shared heading. Each channel has a source name and level readout, a marked horizontal meter, and a volume slider. Speaker-state and overflow controls align at the right of each channel, while shared settings controls occupy the panel footer.
screens.lesson: Repeat the same channel anatomy for names, measurements, sliders, and mute states so users can compare sources without relearning each row.

screens.name: Global audio device settings
screens.layout: A settings dialog has a left category list with Audio selected. The right area separates General settings from Global Audio Devices. Sample-rate and channel selectors occupy the first group; a vertical list of labeled device selectors occupies the second. Confirmation actions align along the lower-right edge outside both groups.
screens.lesson: Separate audio format from device routing, and use consistent labels and selector alignment to clarify which input or output each row configures.

screens.name: Game and webcam production workspace
screens.layout: The preview dominates the studio window and combines a full game capture with a smaller webcam overlay near its lower-left corner. Beneath it, the workspace groups a scene list, a source list, three audio channels, transition controls, and broadcast actions. A source-property strip and status bar bound the lower tools.
screens.lesson: Keep the composed output dominant while aligning source selection and audio controls beneath it, making supporting production tools accessible without competing with the preview.

screens.name: E-commerce dashboard overview
screens.layout: A title and compact action cluster sit above three tabs and two filter controls. The body separates business health from deeper analysis with headings and short descriptions. A wide combination chart shares its row with a narrow metric stack, followed by two equally sized categorical charts.
screens.lesson: Use section headings to explain analytical purpose, and reserve unequal widths for metrics that need different amounts of visual space.

screens.name: Chart beside markdown card editor
screens.layout: A full-width heading precedes two adjacent cards. The larger left card contains a labeled line chart with generous plotting space. The narrower right card exposes multiline markdown text, a visible card boundary, and a compact toolbar above its upper edge. A faint placement grid continues below.
screens.lesson: Keep explanatory content close to its chart, but give editable text a clear boundary and locally positioned editing controls.

screens.name: Dashboard resource links
screens.layout: A page title and small action icons occupy a slim header. Two content sections use a left column for a heading and short explanation, while the right column stacks compact resource rows. Each row has a leading type icon and trailing information control; a rule separates the sections.
screens.lesson: Pair resource groups with concise purpose statements, then align link rows so users can compare destinations without scanning scattered cards.

screens.name: Dashboard with embedded tutorial
screens.layout: A narrow dashboard header places the title on the left and utility icons on the right. Below it, a secondary heading introduces one broad embedded video card. The video thumbnail includes its own title strip, central play control, and corner controls within the dashboard content margins.
screens.lesson: Give embedded media a descriptive section heading and enough width for recognition, while keeping surrounding application controls visually separate.

screens.name: Dashboard chart editing canvas
screens.layout: The dashboard title and tabs form a shallow header above a large placement area. A single line-chart card occupies most of the left side, with a small floating tool strip attached to its upper edge. Unfilled grid cells remain visible to the right and below the chart.
screens.lesson: Expose available placement space around an edited object, and attach contextual tools to that object instead of repeating them across the canvas.

screens.name: Dashboard chart with local tools
screens.layout: An editing banner carries Cancel and Save at the upper right. Below the dashboard title and tab row, one chart fills nearly the entire content width. Its legend sits above the plot, and a compact action strip hovers at the chart corner with a labeled tooltip over one icon.
screens.lesson: Keep page-level saving separate from chart-level editing, and use concise tooltips when a compact icon toolbar needs clarification.

screens.name: Visualization editor with two inspectors
screens.layout: The screen uses three vertical regions: a narrow data list on the left, a central chart preview, and display options on the right. The middle includes chart identity, top actions, field chips beneath the plot, and visualization icons along its bottom. The right inspector groups toggles, a segmented control, and series rows.
screens.lesson: Separate data selection from presentation settings, and keep the preview large enough to assess the consequences of each configuration choice.

screens.name: Dashboard refresh interval menu
screens.layout: A dashboard header and tab row remain visible behind an open menu anchored to a clock icon. The menu has a small heading followed by evenly spaced interval choices, with a checkmark beside the current entry. The dashboard section heading, date filter, and upper edge of a chart remain in view.
screens.lesson: Anchor operational choices near their invoking control and retain enough page context for users to understand the scope of the setting.

screens.name: Dashboard variable multiselect
screens.layout: Variable controls sit in a row immediately above a time-series chart. The open server selector shows selected values as chips inside its field and a checklist below. A selection summary leads the menu, followed by an all option and named servers. The chart and legend remain visible around the menu.
screens.lesson: Combine compact selected-value chips with an explicit checklist when users need to see both current scope and available alternatives.

screens.name: Time-series panel and query editor
screens.layout: Two rows of variable controls and a time-range toolbar precede a broad time-series preview. Below the plot, tabs divide queries, transformations, and alerts. A data-source row and a single query block occupy the lower region, with a monospaced expression spanning most of the width and add actions underneath.
screens.lesson: Place query construction directly below its output and align scope controls above the preview so each region has a distinct responsibility.

screens.name: Branch chooser over repository view
screens.layout: The repository, current branch, and remote action divide the top bar into three blocks. A branch chooser drops below the middle block with two tabs, a filter field, and a New Branch button. Default and recent branches appear under separate headings with names on the left and recency on the right.
screens.lesson: Group frequently revisited options separately from the default choice, and preserve the parent workspace identity while a chooser is open.

screens.name: Diff display settings popover
screens.layout: A file heading sits above a short diff with aligned selection gutters and line numbers. At the upper right, a gear control anchors a settings popover. The popover separates a whitespace checkbox and supporting explanation from two diff-display radio choices, using a clear heading hierarchy within a narrow surface.
screens.lesson: Use a small contextual settings surface for view-specific preferences, and keep explanatory consequences adjacent to the control they qualify.

screens.name: Diff context menu
screens.layout: A file title precedes a diff excerpt with two line-number columns and a wide content column. Expansion indicators bracket the visible excerpt. A small context menu overlaps the selected change near the lower right, offering two vertically stacked actions separated by a rule; the second action is visibly selected.
screens.lesson: Keep context menus short when the selection already supplies scope, and preserve enough surrounding content to explain the action target.

screens.name: Changed files context menu
screens.layout: Changes and History tabs sit above a compact file list with a count row and selection boxes. Two file rows are selected. A tall context menu overlaps the list and groups discard, ignore, inclusion, path, and opening actions with separators. Action labels explicitly refer to the selected file count.
screens.lesson: Write bulk-action labels with their selection scope and group related commands so destructive and navigational choices are not visually intermingled.

screens.name: Changes list and commit composer
screens.layout: A narrow sidebar places Changes and History tabs above a filter and one changed-file row. A large open region separates the file list from a bottom-aligned commit composer. The composer contains an avatar, summary field, multiline description, small auxiliary controls, and a full-width commit button with the file count.
screens.lesson: Anchor the commitment form predictably beneath the selection area, and repeat the affected item count in the final action label.

screens.name: Repository clean-state guidance
screens.layout: A large clean-state heading and one explanatory sentence lead the panel, with a small illustration at the right. A broad recommendation box below pairs a task heading, explanatory text, and shortcut hints on the left with a prominent split action button on the right.
screens.lesson: Explain what an empty state means, then offer one relevant next step with its action placed beside the supporting rationale.

screens.name: Raycast account and subscriptions
screens.layout: A desktop settings window uses an icon-labeled sidebar and a wider detail pane. The account item is selected at the top of navigation. A centered avatar and identity lead the detail pane, followed by grouped subscription rows with trailing statuses and an account section containing management and sign-out actions.
screens.lesson: Lead account settings with identity, align subscription status consistently, and separate account actions from the descriptive plan information above.

screens.name: Spotlight keyboard shortcuts sheet
screens.layout: A large shortcut sheet overlays a dimmed Keyboard settings window. The sheet has its own category sidebar on the left and a wide option area on the right. Three shortcut rows align checkboxes, action names, and key combinations beneath instructions. Restore Defaults and Done occupy opposite ends of the footer.
screens.lesson: For complex preference dialogs, preserve category navigation and align shortcut assignments in a dedicated column separate from action labels.

screens.name: Apple Intelligence and Siri settings
screens.layout: A searchable category sidebar occupies the left of a desktop window. The detail pane starts with a page heading and an introductory feature group. A second section collects Siri controls in aligned rows with values and switches at the right, followed by explanatory privacy text and a separate secondary button.
screens.lesson: Group capability switches separately from detailed preferences, and keep privacy explanations near the settings that determine how the capability is used.

screens.name: Launcher search preferences
screens.layout: A settings sidebar highlights Launcher while the detail pane presents a vertical sequence of preference groups. The upper group aligns short labels and descriptions with trailing values. A search customization group contains two switches, followed by a fallback-command section with an add row and an existing command entry.
screens.lesson: Organize preferences by the decision users make, and use consistent trailing alignment even when rows mix switches, values, and navigation.

screens.name: Fallback command search menu
screens.layout: The Launcher settings pane remains visible with search customization above a fallback-command list. A compact menu extends downward from the add-command row. It begins with a short typed query, then lists matching commands with leading icons and one selected row. The settings sidebar continues to identify the active category.
screens.lesson: Use a focused command search beside the configuration list it modifies, preserving the parent setting as context for the selection.

screens.name: Shortcut categories and filter
screens.layout: The Shortcuts category is selected in the left settings sidebar. The right pane begins with a search field and category selector on one line, then stacks five broad category rows. Each row pairs a leading icon and disclosure mark with a small trailing selection indicator; substantial open space follows the list.
screens.lesson: Keep search and scope controls together, and use consistent category rows before exposing a potentially much larger set of individual shortcuts.

screens.name: Keyboard behavior preferences
screens.layout: The Keyboard section uses the same sidebar and detail split as the surrounding settings. The main pane stacks behavior rows with labels and smaller descriptions at the left, and switches or current values at the right. A lower group collects modifier-related options, separated from the preceding navigation-key settings.
screens.lesson: Preserve explanatory room for unfamiliar keyboard preferences while aligning current values so experienced users can scan their configuration quickly.

screens.name: Advanced export and connection settings
screens.layout: A left sidebar highlights Advanced. The detail pane starts with two general preference rows, then introduces Export and Connection sections. Export contains a masked passphrase field and backup schedule value. Connection presents a proxy switch and certificate file button, with brief explanations beneath the associated labels.
screens.lesson: Use section headings to separate advanced concerns, and pair unusual inputs such as certificates or passphrases with concise purpose statements.

screens.name: AI settings overview
screens.layout: The AI category is selected in a long settings sidebar. A centered icon, title, and subtitle introduce the detail pane, with an information icon and switch in its top corner. Three navigation rows display agents, commands, and extensions with trailing counts, followed by the start of a personalization section.
screens.lesson: Introduce a broad feature area with a compact overview, then expose its subcollections through rows with consistent counts and disclosure affordances.

screens.name: AI conversation preferences
screens.layout: A scrolled AI settings pane retains its title and master switch while the sidebar identifies the feature. A General section aligns conversation options and descriptions with trailing values. Below it, an API Keys group has explanatory text, a small add control, and a muted empty-state row; a Commands section begins below.
screens.lesson: Keep feature identity visible in long preference panes, and distinguish an empty configuration collection from ordinary editable preference rows.

screens.name: Raycast extension store results
screens.layout: A floating launcher window places a broad search input and category controls across the top. Six extension rows pair recognizable icons with names and one-line descriptions, while compact metadata aligns at the right. A selected row spans the list width. A footer identifies Store and displays detail and action shortcuts.
screens.lesson: Give each result a stable name-description structure and align metadata separately, with the active result and its available actions visibly connected.

screens.name: Screenshot extension preferences
screens.layout: A long extension sidebar highlights Screenshots beside a detail pane led by a centered icon, title, and description. A Column Count group presents four miniature grid previews with numeric labels. Below it, Search Scopes lists folder paths under explanatory text and a small add control aligned to the group heading.
screens.lesson: Use small structural previews for layout choices, then separate those visual preferences from the resource locations that define content scope.

screens.name: Visual query construction steps
screens.layout: Three broad steps are stacked vertically: Data, Filter, and Summarize. Each step contains compact chips within a large horizontal region, with a small triangular control at the far right. Summarize divides aggregation from grouping into two columns. A row of operation tiles and a Visualize button finish the working area.
screens.lesson: Make query structure readable as labeled stages, and distinguish aggregation from grouping spatially instead of relying only on specialized terminology.

screens.name: Query builder with table preview
screens.layout: Data, Filter, and Summarize rows form the upper portion of the query builder. Directly below the summary stage, a bordered Preview area shows a compact two-column table with four result rows and a close control. A Sort stage follows beneath the preview, keeping the table embedded within the surrounding construction steps.
screens.lesson: Place a small result preview beside the stage it explains, preserving the query sequence so users can relate output to configuration.

screens.name: Starting data chooser
screens.layout: A prominent title introduces the starting-data surface. Beneath a small Data label, a broad search region spans the available width. A compact menu sits below its left edge, listing a database and analytics collection with icons and disclosure arrows, followed by a separated Browse all option.
screens.lesson: Offer search and structured browsing in the same chooser, using clear resource-type icons and a distinct route to the complete collection.

screens.name: Custom column formula editor
screens.layout: The query builder remains visible behind a large expression panel attached to the Custom column stage. The panel contains a line-number gutter, one formula near the top, and two small tools at the right. Its footer aligns the column name on the left with Cancel and Done on the right.
screens.lesson: Give formulas sufficient editing area while keeping the resulting field name and completion controls visible within the same contextual panel.

screens.name: Visual query with generated SQL pane
screens.layout: A shallow title bar spans the screen with SQL visibility and save actions at the right. The content divides into a visual query builder on the left and an SQL pane on the right. The builder contains labeled stages and operation tiles; the SQL pane has its own heading and a numbered monospaced statement.
screens.lesson: Show alternate representations side by side when comparison is the task, giving each pane its own clear heading and ample readable width.

screens.name: Chart exploration menu
screens.layout: A dense vertical bar chart fills the surface with labeled axes and time controls centered beneath it. A floating menu overlaps the plotted bars, offering account inspection, a finer time grouping, breakout, and insights. A final filter section presents four small comparison buttons in a horizontal row.
screens.lesson: Place chart-specific exploration choices near the selected data context, and separate navigation actions from compact value-comparison controls.

screens.name: Relative date filter choices
screens.layout: A date-filter menu extends downward from the filter stage of a visual query builder. A back arrow and field name head the menu, followed by common relative periods arranged in short groups. Rules separate recent-day choices, month-based choices, and more specific date options. Other query stages remain partly visible behind it.
screens.lesson: Group date choices by time scale and keep custom or exclusion options separate, so frequent selections remain easy to find.

screens.name: Custom filter expression dialog
screens.layout: A compact expression dialog overlays the query builder near its Filter stage. The header includes a back arrow and a title. A persistent Expression label precedes a single code-like input spanning the dialog width. Cancel and Done sit together in the lower right, leaving generous space between the field and actions.
screens.lesson: For short expressions, keep the input focused and retain a clear return path, with completion controls consistently grouped at the lower edge.

screens.name: Named aggregate expression dialog
screens.layout: The Summarize row stays visible behind a dialog containing an aggregate expression. Inside the dialog, an Expression field precedes a separately labeled Name field. The expression uses monospaced text while the name uses ordinary input styling. Cancel and Update align at the bottom right beneath the two-field stack.
screens.lesson: Separate a computed expression from its human-readable name, and use persistent labels so both purposes remain clear after values are entered.

screens.name: Sequential aggregation stages
screens.layout: Two Summarize stages are stacked with ample vertical spacing. Each stage places its aggregation region on the left and grouping region on the right, joined by the word by. Small operation icons sit beneath the first stage, while the second includes a removal control and an empty grouping prompt.
screens.lesson: Repeat a consistent stage anatomy for chained transformations, and distinguish an intentionally empty grouping choice from a configured aggregation chip.

screens.name: Chart grouping inspector
screens.layout: A multi-series line chart occupies roughly three quarters of the surface, with legend labels above and time controls below. A narrow right inspector separates Summarize by from Group by. Selected grouping chips appear above a searchable field list organized under source headings, with small data-type icons beside each field.
screens.lesson: Keep active grouping choices above the available field list, and preserve a large chart area for evaluating the resulting comparison.

screens.name: Histogram and numeric field inspector
screens.layout: A wide histogram occupies the left side, with readable count and price axes and few distractions around the bars. A narrow inspector on the right shows a vertically ordered field list grouped by source. The selected numeric field appears as a full-width chip with its binning value and a removal mark.
screens.lesson: Expose the chosen numeric field and its grouping treatment alongside the histogram, keeping raw field browsing secondary to the plotted distribution.

screens.name: Join type selector in query builder
screens.layout: A Data stage sits above a Join data stage divided into a table relationship on the left and matching columns on the right. A small menu opens beneath the join symbol with three labeled join choices and matching icons. Operation tiles and a Visualize button remain visible below the join configuration.
screens.lesson: Place relationship-type choices directly on the relationship they describe, and pair specialized icons with explicit labels for clarity.

screens.name: Data source modal for joins
screens.layout: A modal sits over a dimmed query builder with a title and close control in its header. A full-width search input precedes three tabs. Below them, a left list shows table names and icons with one selected row, while a broad empty region to the right preserves space for deeper browsing.
screens.lesson: Combine search with source-type tabs in larger choosers, and make the selected item unmistakable without obscuring the parent task.

screens.name: Two joins in a visual query
screens.layout: A source Data row spans the top. Two Join data rows follow, each repeating a table pair and relationship symbol on the left with matching column chips on the right. Each match includes a small plus control. Shared spacing and alignment make the two relationships appear as successive steps of one query.
screens.lesson: Reuse the same visual grammar for multiple relationships, aligning table pairs and match criteria so complex queries remain structurally comparable.

screens.name: Join with multiple matching columns
screens.layout: The Data stage appears above a single Join data stage. The lower stage divides its table relationship on the left from a taller condition area on the right. Two matching-column chips are stacked with an and label between them, individual removal marks, and an add control at the lower right.
screens.lesson: When conditions multiply, stack them within one relationship group and make the logical connector explicit instead of relying on proximity.

screens.name: Join comparison operator menu
screens.layout: A Join data row shows its table pair at the left and a comparison condition at the right. A narrow operator menu drops from the small symbol between the two field names. Six comparison symbols are stacked vertically, with the current choice emphasized. Operation tiles and a Visualize action remain visible underneath.
screens.lesson: Keep operator selection attached to the exact condition it modifies, and make the selected operator visually distinct within the compact list.

screens.name: Query stages with intermediate previews
screens.layout: A vertical query sequence begins with Reviews data and an average-rating summary. A one-row preview appears immediately below that stage. A join to Reviews follows, then a wider preview table with the average and several review fields. Each preview has a small heading and close mark within the surrounding step sequence.
screens.lesson: For multi-stage data work, show intermediate output at meaningful boundaries so users can inspect transformations without losing the overall sequence.

screens.name: Expression help and validation context
screens.layout: A custom-expression editor overlays the Summarize stage, with a line number and partially entered function. A help card overlaps the editor and displays a signature, parameter explanations, a code example, and a documentation link. An error strip remains partly visible behind the card, above a footer with completion actions.
screens.lesson: Place function guidance close to the expression, but ensure validation and completion controls remain discoverable when supplementary help is open.

screens.name: Expression editor with function browser
screens.layout: A custom-expression panel spans the lower part of the query builder. Its large left area is a line-numbered editor with a short input hint and footer actions. A narrower right pane contains a search field, category heading, and a vertical list of function names followed by brief descriptions.
screens.lesson: Give reference material its own adjacent pane when users need to compose and browse simultaneously, preserving room for the expression itself.

screens.name: Table preview with variable query
screens.layout: A variable chip group and time-range toolbar sit above a two-column result table. Below the table, query and transformation tabs lead into a data-source row and an expanded query configuration. The lower form places scenario, string input, and alias on one horizontal line. Documentation outlines emphasize selected controls and one table row.
screens.lesson: Align query inputs beneath their result preview, and use real field hierarchy rather than copying documentation callouts into the target interface.

screens.name: Dashboard link configuration
screens.layout: A New link heading and short description introduce a single-column form. Title, type, URL, tooltip, and icon fields are stacked with persistent labels. An Options heading separates three checkboxes from the primary fields. A Back to list button sits below the options at the left edge.
screens.lesson: Separate destination identity from optional link behavior, keeping labels persistent and related checkboxes together below the main input sequence.

screens.name: Empty dashboard editor
screens.layout: A largely empty dashboard canvas retains a top toolbar and a narrow right tool rail. The center presents a small icon, a dashboard creation heading, and a broad prompt composer. A divider introduces an alternative manual path with an Add visualization button below. Substantial open space surrounds the central choices.
screens.lesson: Give a blank workspace a clear starting point and a visible manual alternative, while keeping persistent editing tools at the perimeter.

screens.name: Visualization suggestions panel
screens.layout: A narrow selector has two tabs at the top and a search field immediately beneath. The body begins with a Time series category label and a large preview card containing axes and a sample line. Another preview starts below the fold, and a scrollbar on the right indicates a longer collection.
screens.lesson: Use substantial previews when users choose visual forms, with search and categories helping them navigate beyond the first visible option.

screens.name: Dashboard options beside chart
screens.layout: A variable row and time toolbar span the top of an editing workspace. A single area-chart panel occupies the left, while a wide Dashboard inspector fills the right. The inspector contains a settings button, title and description inputs, a layout selector, and collapsed configuration sections. A slim tool rail borders the far right.
screens.lesson: Keep document metadata and layout configuration together in an inspector, preserving the chart as a visible reference while settings are considered.

screens.name: Dashboard content outline
screens.layout: A dashboard row and nested tab sit above one area-chart panel on the left. A Content outline pane occupies the right, with a search field followed by an indented tree. The tree separates filters, variables, annotations, and links from nested content groups. A compact vertical tool rail remains along the outer edge.
screens.lesson: Offer an outline when nesting becomes difficult to read on the canvas, and mirror content hierarchy through indentation and concise labels.

screens.name: Dashboard layout controls in context
screens.layout: A dashboard group contains two neighboring visualization panels beneath a shared heading. Add panel and Group panels controls sit below the group, followed by row-level actions. A small contextual menu near a panel corner presents layout choices. Documentation rectangles draw attention to the group indicator and this menu.
screens.lesson: Place layout tools at the level they affect, distinguishing controls for an individual panel, a panel group, and the surrounding row.

screens.name: Dashboard add-content panel
screens.layout: A narrow Add panel has a header with back and close controls. A large preview-like panel insertion tile leads the content. Group layouts follows with two broad choices, then Dashboard controls presents four stacked insertion options. A slim icon rail sits at the right, and a documentation outline surrounds the controls group.
screens.lesson: Group insertion choices by their role in the document, separating content, structural containers, and controls instead of presenting one undifferentiated menu.

screens.name: Dashboard control placement inspector
screens.layout: A tall Dashboard inspector groups filters, variables, annotations, and links into collapsible sections. Expanded groups divide their contents by placement, with counts in the subheadings and individual rows below. Small add buttons span each group width. A scrollbar and a separate icon rail run along the right side.
screens.lesson: When controls can occupy several regions, organize configuration by both control type and placement, with counts showing the current distribution.

screens.name: Nested dashboard groups
screens.layout: A compact time toolbar precedes a dashboard organized into nested rows and tabs. Within the active tab, one row holds an area chart and pie chart at equal widths. A second row pairs a wide horizontal bar chart with a narrow headline value. Indented headings and disclosure marks communicate the nesting.
screens.lesson: Use nesting only when it reflects meaningful analytical groups, and vary panel proportions according to the information each visualization needs.

screens.name: Table panel inside selected group
screens.layout: A dotted selection boundary encloses a labeled row containing a large table panel. The table aligns state names at the left and year-based numeric columns to the right. Add panel and Group panels buttons sit inside the selected region beneath the table, while New row and Ungroup rows sit outside it.
screens.lesson: Use a clear container boundary to explain scope, placing group actions inside the selection and broader structural actions outside it.

screens.name: Mixed visualization dashboard grid
screens.layout: A time-range toolbar and row heading lead a four-panel dashboard. The upper pair combines a time-series chart with a grouped horizontal bar chart. Below, a pie chart occupies a smaller left panel while a large numerical metric takes the wider right panel. Shared gutters align the panel edges across the two rows.
screens.lesson: Let panel size communicate analytical priority, balancing supporting distributions and trends against a deliberately prominent headline value.

screens.name: Metrics dashboard with section filters
screens.layout: Global data-source and instance controls sit beside the time toolbar above two tabs. The dashboard body has two named sections, each with a local filter row followed by two side-by-side charts. Legends align beneath the plots, while documentation outlines emphasize the local filter controls within their respective sections.
screens.lesson: Distinguish global scope from section-specific constraints through placement, keeping each local filter immediately above the charts it qualifies.
